laws.title: Driving Under the Influence of Electronics (E-DUI)
laws.subtitle: RCW 46.61.672 — $136 first offense + $234 second
laws.fullDescription: Washington State bans holding or using a handheld device while driving, including at stop lights. The 'E-DUI' law treats distracted driving with similar seriousness as impaired driving. Hands-free calling is permitted.
laws.penalty: 1st offense: $136. 2nd offense within 5 years: $234 + reported to insurance.
exceptions: Emergency 911 calls
Completely stopped in a safe location off the roadway
Law enforcement / first responders

quiz.q: Washington State's 'E-DUI' law second-offense fine?
quiz.explanation: A second handheld device violation in Washington State within 5 years carries a $234 fine, reported to the driver's insurance.

laws.title: Recreational Cannabis — I-502 (21+, 1 oz limit)
laws.subtitle: RCW 69.50 — Legal with public consumption restrictions
laws.fullDescription: Washington State legalized recreational cannabis in 2012 (Initiative 502). Adults 21+ may possess up to 1 oz of usable cannabis, 16 oz cannabis-infused product (solid), 72 oz (liquid). Cannabis must be purchased from licensed retailers. Public consumption is still illegal (fine $103).
laws.penalty: Public consumption: $103 civil infraction. Driving under influence of cannabis: DUI charges.
exceptions: Cannot consume in public spaces, parks, or vehicles
Federal lands (national parks, federal buildings) enforce federal prohibition

quiz.q: Maximum cannabis possession for adults 21+ in Washington State?
quiz.explanation: Washington State adults 21+ may legally possess up to 1 oz of usable cannabis purchased from licensed retailers.

laws.title: Pacific Northwest Culture — Outdoors, Rain Pride & Coffee
laws.subtitle: Seattle Freeze, fleece jackets, and strong opinions about coffee
laws.fullDescription: Pacific Northwesterners are outdoors-oriented year-round — hiking, kayaking, skiing even in rain. The 'Seattle Freeze' (initial reserve with strangers) is real: people are polite but initially guarded. Fleece and REI gear are worn to upscale restaurants. Coffee culture is intense — never order a drip coffee at a local coffee shop. Environmental consciousness is strong. 'Seattle Nice' means indirect politeness rather than effusive friendliness.
laws.penalty: No legal penalty — complaining about rain or showing disdain for outdoor culture will mark you as an outsider.
exceptions: Eastern Washington (east of Cascades) has a different, more agricultural and conservative culture
Portland, Oregon has its own distinct quirky identity

quiz.q: What is the 'Seattle Freeze'?
options: The tendency of Seattle locals to be initially reserved with new people
quiz.explanation: The 'Seattle Freeze' refers to the tendency of Seattle residents to be polite but initially reserved and slow to form close friendships.

laws.title: Campfire Rules — Fire Restrictions and Burn Bans
laws.subtitle: DNR and Forest Service seasonal bans — Violations are criminal
laws.fullDescription: Washington State's Department of Natural Resources and the US Forest Service impose tiered fire restrictions in summer (typically June–September): Level 1 restricts campfires in some areas, Level 2 bans all campfires in backcountry, Level 3 closes areas entirely. Violations are criminal offences. Camp stoves using gas canisters may still be permitted under Level 1 and 2. Always check current restrictions before going out — conditions change daily. Washington also has strict 'Discover Pass' requirements for parking at most state lands.
laws.penalty: Illegal campfire during ban: criminal misdemeanour + fine up to $5,000. Causing a wildfire: full suppression cost liability (potentially millions). No Discover Pass: $99 fine.
exceptions: Designated campground fire rings if not under a Level 2+ ban
Gas camp stoves with on/off valves allowed under many restrictions
laws.sourceLabel: Washington Department of Natural Resources — Fire Restrictions

quiz.q: What does a Level 2 fire restriction in Washington State prohibit?
quiz.explanation: A Level 2 fire restriction in Washington State bans all campfires in backcountry areas — violations are criminal misdemeanours carrying fines up to $5,000.

laws.title: Death Penalty Abolished — Washington Supreme Court 2018
laws.subtitle: State v. Gregory — Death penalty declared unconstitutional
laws.fullDescription: Washington State's Supreme Court ruled in State v. Gregory (2018) that the death penalty is unconstitutional under the Washington State Constitution, finding it is 'imposed arbitrarily.' Governor Jay Inslee had already declared a moratorium on executions in 2014. The 8 inmates on death row had their sentences converted to life without parole. Washington was the 20th US state to abolish the death penalty and is considered among the nation's most progressive on criminal justice reform. Washington also abolished solitary confinement for most inmates in 2021.
laws.penalty: No death penalty — maximum punishment for aggravated first-degree murder: life without parole.
exceptions: Federal courts still have jurisdiction over federal capital crimes committed in Washington
Federal prisons in Washington still operate under federal law
laws.sourceLabel: State v. Gregory (2018) — Washington Supreme Court

quiz.q: Why did Washington State's Supreme Court abolish the death penalty in 2018?
options: It was found unconstitutional — imposed arbitrarily under the state constitution
quiz.explanation: Washington's Supreme Court in State v. Gregory (2018) ruled the death penalty unconstitutional under Washington's constitution, finding it was 'imposed arbitrarily' — sentences were converted to life without parole.

laws.title: Washington State Salmon Protection — Puget Sound Laws
laws.subtitle: Washington Hydraulic Code — Protecting salmon spawning habitat
laws.fullDescription: Washington State has extraordinarily strict salmon and fish habitat protection laws. Under the Hydraulic Project Approval (HPA) requirement, any work in or near Washington's waterways — from building a dock to removing a log from a stream — requires an HPA permit from the Washington Department of Fish and Wildlife (WDFW). Salmon runs are considered critical for tribal treaty rights, commercial fisheries, and ecosystems. Endangered salmon species (Chinook, Coho, Sockeye) are federally protected under the Endangered Species Act. Even lawn chemicals that run off into waterways threatening salmon can trigger enforcement.
laws.penalty: Working in waterways without HPA: civil penalty up to $100/day + criminal misdemeanor. ESA violations (harming listed salmon): federal penalties up to $50,000/day.
exceptions: Normal agricultural irrigation with appropriate permits
Emergency repairs with after-the-fact HPA application
Small dock installations under certain size thresholds
laws.sourceLabel: Washington Hydraulic Code — WDFW Hydraulic Project Approval

quiz.q: What do Washington State landowners need before doing any work in or near waterways, including removing a log?
options: A Hydraulic Project Approval (HPA) permit from WDFW
Army Corps of Engineers permit only
quiz.explanation: Washington's Hydraulic Code requires an HPA permit from WDFW before any work in or near waterways — even removing a log from a stream — to protect critical salmon habitat and tribal treaty fishing rights.

laws.title: Washington Outdoor Recreation Laws — No-Discover Pass = Fine; Wildfire Liability
laws.subtitle: Recreation Access Pass — State parks require Discover Pass; campfire rules strict
laws.fullDescription: Washington State requires a Discover Pass ($30/year or $10/day) for all motorised vehicle access to state parks, state forests, and wildlife areas. Parking at a trailhead without a Discover Pass results in a $99 infraction. Washington also has strict campfire laws: during high fire danger periods (typically July–September), campfires are banned at many dispersed camping areas. Starting a wildfire through negligence in Washington can result in state costs billed to the responsible party — Washington has billed individuals millions of dollars for wildfire suppression. Washington's state ferry system (WSF) is the largest in the USA and has strict rules about remaining in vehicles on car decks during crossings.
laws.penalty: No Discover Pass: $99 infraction. Illegal campfire causing wildfire: civil liability for full suppression costs ($1M+). Remaining in vehicle on ferry car deck: safety violation + removal.
exceptions: Disabled American Veterans (DAV) and certain veterans receive free Discover Passes
Department of Natural Resources permit-holders

quiz.q: What is the daily fee for a Washington State Discover Pass required to park at state park trailheads?
quiz.explanation: Washington State's Discover Pass costs $10 per day (or $30 per year) — required for all motorised vehicle access to state parks, state forests, and wildlife areas. Parking without one results in a $99 infraction.

laws.title: Orca Protection — Puget Sound's Southern Resident Orcas Are Critically Endangered
laws.subtitle: Marine Mammal Protection Act + WA State Orca Act 2018 — 200-yard minimum distance
laws.fullDescription: Washington State's Southern Resident Killer Whale (orca) population is critically endangered — only around 73 individuals remain in 2024. Washington's Orca Protection Act (2018) and federal Marine Mammal Protection Act set strict rules: a minimum 200-yard (183-metre) approach distance for all boats, no boat within 400 yards of the path of an orca, kayaks and paddleboards must stop engines. Whale watching vessels must be licensed by NOAA and the Washington Department of Fish and Wildlife. The primary threat to Southern Residents is prey depletion (Chinook salmon) and vessel noise, which interferes with echolocation. The Pacific Whale Watch Association maintains voluntary best-practice codes that exceed legal minimums.
laws.penalty: Approaching orcas within 200 yards: fine up to $100,000 under Marine Mammal Protection Act. Repeated violations: federal prosecution.
exceptions: NOAA and state research vessels with scientific research permits
Emergency rescue vessels responding to a distress call
laws.sourceLabel: Washington Department of Fish and Wildlife — Orca Protection

quiz.q: Approximately how many Southern Resident Killer Whales (orcas) remain in Washington State's Puget Sound as of 2024?
quiz.explanation: Only approximately 73 Southern Resident Killer Whales remain as of 2024 — critically endangered due to prey depletion, vessel noise, and pollution. Washington State's Orca Protection Act (2018) established strict boat approach distances to reduce disturbance.

laws.title: Salmon Recovery Laws — Culverts, Tribal Rights, and the $4 Billion Road Fix
laws.subtitle: Washington State was ordered by courts to fix fish-blocking culverts after tribal treaty lawsuits
laws.fullDescription: Washington State's salmon crisis prompted one of the most significant environmental legal battles in US history. Tribes with treaty fishing rights (signed 1855) successfully argued in federal court that state-owned road culverts blocking salmon passage violated treaty rights — the 9th Circuit upheld this in 2016, and the US Supreme Court affirmed in 2018 by equally divided 4-4 ruling. The ruling ordered Washington to fix approximately 1,000 culverts blocking salmon at an estimated cost of $4 billion over 17 years. Additionally, Washington's 1999 Forest and Fish Agreement created a unique system where timber companies must maintain riparian buffers to protect salmon-bearing streams. The Southern Resident Killer Whale (orca) population — which depends on Chinook salmon — has only about 70 individuals remaining.
laws.penalty: Violating salmon habitat protection orders: fines up to $10,000/day + injunctions. Culvert violations: contempt of federal court. Unauthorized salmon harvest outside treaty season: criminal charges.
exceptions: Tribal nations have treaty-protected fishing rights in their usual and accustomed places
Hatchery salmon may be harvested under different rules than wild salmon
Emergency WDFW-authorized commercial harvest in specific overabundant runs
laws.sourceLabel: Washington Dept of Fish & Wildlife — Salmon Recovery Programs

quiz.q: Why was Washington State ordered by federal courts to fix fish-blocking road culverts at a cost of $4 billion?
options: Environmental Protection Agency regulations required it
Indigenous tribes with 1855 treaty fishing rights successfully argued the culverts violated their treaty
A ballot initiative passed by Washington voters mandated the fixes
Federal highway safety regulations required culvert upgrades
quiz.explanation: Indigenous tribes holding 1855 treaty-based fishing rights successfully argued in federal court that Washington State's road culverts blocking salmon passage violated their treaty rights to fish at 'usual and accustomed' places. The Supreme Court upheld the ruling in 2018, ordering Washington to fix ~1,000 culverts at an estimated $4 billion cost.

laws.title: Washington's Climate Commitment Act — Cap and Trade with Carbon Allowance Auctions
laws.subtitle: Washington's 2021 CCA created a mandatory cap-and-invest program for large industrial emitters
laws.fullDescription: Washington State's Climate Commitment Act (HB 1091, 2021) created one of the US's most ambitious cap-and-trade programs for large emitters (100,000+ metric tonnes CO2/year). Companies must purchase carbon allowances at quarterly auctions; the cap declines annually toward 95% reduction by 2050. Revenue goes to clean transportation, clean buildings, and environmental justice communities. California and Quebec's linked cap-and-trade market provides the pricing framework. In 2023, Washington's carbon auctions raised over $2 billion — among the highest prices globally ($50–60/tonne CO2). A Republican-backed referendum (Initiative 2117) to repeal the CCA was placed on the November 2024 ballot. The program links with California's cap-and-trade system.
laws.penalty: Failing to surrender sufficient carbon allowances: $50 per tonne shortfall above permit cost + mandatory compliance. Misrepresenting emissions data: criminal fraud + significant fines under ECY enforcement.
exceptions: Utilities passing costs to customers under PUC oversight
Agricultural and natural lands have offset credit programs
Small businesses below emission threshold exempt
laws.sourceLabel: Washington Dept of Ecology — Climate Commitment Act

quiz.q: How much revenue did Washington State's carbon cap-and-trade auctions raise in 2023?
quiz.explanation: Washington State's carbon cap-and-trade auctions raised over $2 billion in 2023 — making it one of the world's most valuable carbon markets in terms of per-tonne price ($50–60/tonne CO2) and total revenue. Funds go to clean transportation, building decarbonization, and environmental justice communities.

laws.title: Death with Dignity Act
laws.subtitle: Washington became the second US state to legalize physician-assisted death in 2008
laws.fullDescription: Washington's Death with Dignity Act (Initiative 1000, 2008) allows terminally ill Washington adults with a prognosis of 6 months or less to request a lethal prescription from a physician. Requirements include two oral requests separated by 15 days, one written request, a mental health evaluation if concerns arise, and confirmation of terminal diagnosis by two physicians. Patients self-administer the medication. The law has faced ongoing legislative refinements — the 15-day waiting period was reduced to 7 days in 2023. Oregon was the first state (1997); 10+ US states now have similar laws.
laws.penalty: Coercing someone to use the Act: criminal liability. Physicians who participate face no criminal or civil liability when following the Act's requirements. Forging requests: felony.
exceptions: Patients must be Washington state residents
Only physicians licensed in Washington may participate
Healthcare providers and facilities may opt out of participation on moral grounds
laws.sourceLabel: Washington State DOH — Death with Dignity

quiz.q: How long must terminally ill patients wait between their first oral request and receiving a prescription under Washington's Death with Dignity Act (as of 2023)?
quiz.explanation: Washington's Death with Dignity Act originally required a 15-day waiting period between oral requests, but this was reduced to 7 days in 2023 to reduce suffering for patients with rapidly progressing terminal illness.

laws.title: WA Cares Fund — Mandatory Long-Term Care Insurance
laws.subtitle: Washington became the first US state to create a mandatory public long-term care insurance program
laws.fullDescription: Washington's WA Cares Fund, enacted in 2019 and collecting premiums from 2023, is the first mandatory public long-term care insurance program in the United States. Workers pay 0.58% of wages into the fund; in exchange, they receive up to $36,500 lifetime benefit (indexed to inflation) for qualifying long-term care needs after a 10-year vesting period. The law addresses a massive gap: two-thirds of Americans will eventually need long-term care, yet private insurance is prohibitively expensive and Medicaid requires near-total asset depletion first. The program faced a political backlash: tens of thousands rushed to buy private insurance to opt out before the deadline.
laws.penalty: Employers who fail to withhold WA Cares premiums: penalties equal to the unpaid premiums. Workers who improperly claim exemptions: repayment of avoided premiums plus interest.
exceptions: Workers who purchased qualifying private long-term care insurance before November 2021 may opt out
Military veterans with 70%+ service-connected disability rating are exempt
Non-Washington workers employed by Washington employers pay but cannot access benefits unless they move to Washington

quiz.q: What makes Washington State's WA Cares Fund historically significant in the United States?
options: It is the first state pension fund for all workers
It is the first mandatory public long-term care insurance program in the US
It provides universal health insurance for all state residents
It is the world's largest sovereign wealth fund
quiz.explanation: Washington's WA Cares Fund is the first mandatory public long-term care insurance program in the United States — a groundbreaking attempt to address the massive coverage gap that leaves most Americans unable to afford long-term care.

laws.title: Death with Dignity Act: Legal Physician-Assisted Dying
laws.subtitle: Washington allows terminally ill patients to request a lethal prescription — one of the first US states to do so
laws.fullDescription: Washington's Death with Dignity Act (RCW 70.245), passed by voter initiative in 2008, allows terminally ill Washington residents with fewer than 6 months to live to request a prescription for life-ending medication from their physician. The patient must be an adult, mentally competent, and make two verbal requests 15 days apart plus one written request witnessed by two people. The physician must inform them of alternatives, and a consulting physician must confirm the diagnosis and prognosis. The law explicitly states that death under this act does not constitute suicide for insurance purposes, and participation by physicians is entirely voluntary.
laws.penalty: No criminal penalty for following the law's procedures. Forging or coercing a request: Class A felony
exceptions: Patients must self-administer the medication — physicians cannot administer it
No requirement for physicians to participate; they may decline on conscience grounds

quiz.q: How many days must separate the two verbal requests under Washington's Death with Dignity Act?
quiz.explanation: Washington's Death with Dignity Act requires a 15-day waiting period between the two verbal requests, designed to ensure the decision is persistent and not impulsive.

laws.title: Washington's Cap-and-Invest Program: Nation's Most Aggressive Carbon Pricing
laws.subtitle: Washington launched the US's most ambitious state-level carbon market in 2023 — then voters repealed it in 2024
laws.fullDescription: Washington State's Climate Commitment Act (2021) created a 'cap-and-invest' carbon pricing program that launched in January 2023 — requiring large greenhouse gas emitters to purchase allowances for their emissions. The program raised over $1.8 billion in its first year, funding clean energy, electric vehicles, and environmental justice programs. However, the carbon cost added approximately 40–50 cents to gasoline prices, fueling public backlash. In November 2024, voters passed Initiative 2117, repealing the program — a major setback for state-level climate policy. Washington became a case study in how carbon pricing's economic visibility can doom even well-designed programs. The state retained other climate laws but lost its centerpiece carbon market.
laws.penalty: Emitting above allowance levels without purchasing sufficient credits: civil penalties up to $10,000 per metric ton of excess emissions
exceptions: Agricultural operations, small businesses, and some industrial facilities had phase-in provisions
The repeal (I-2117) does not affect Washington's clean fuel standard or building electrification requirements
laws.sourceLabel: Washington State Dept. of Ecology – Climate Commitment Act

quiz.q: What happened to Washington State's cap-and-invest carbon program in November 2024?
options: It was expanded to cover more sectors
Voters passed an initiative repealing it
The legislature suspended it for two years
It was transferred to a regional multi-state system
quiz.explanation: Washington voters passed Initiative 2117 in November 2024, repealing the Climate Commitment Act's cap-and-invest carbon market — citing the 40–50 cent per gallon gasoline cost increase it caused. The repeal was a major setback for state-level carbon pricing models.

laws.title: Boldt Decision: Washington Tribes' Treaty Right to Half the Salmon
laws.subtitle: A 1974 federal court ruling gave Washington tribes the right to 50% of the salmon harvest — reshaping fisheries law across the Pacific Northwest
laws.fullDescription: Judge George Boldt's 1974 ruling in United States v. Washington (the 'Boldt Decision') interpreted 19th-century treaties between Washington tribes and the US government to mean that tribes had a right to 50% of the harvestable salmon and steelhead passing through their traditional fishing areas. The ruling was upheld by the Supreme Court in 1979. It transformed Pacific Northwest fisheries management, created the co-management system where state and tribal agencies jointly set fish runs and quotas, and established Washington's 29 federally recognized tribes as co-managers of natural resources. A 2018 Ninth Circuit ruling extended the decision to require Washington State to maintain culverts (road drainage pipes) so fish can migrate — at an estimated $3.8 billion cost to the state.
laws.penalty: Fishing in violation of tribal-state co-management agreements: federal and state violations. Blocking fish passage through culverts: federal injunction requiring compliance with state infrastructure upgrade mandates
exceptions: Tribal members can fish in their traditional areas under treaty rights that supersede state season limits
Commercial fishing outside tribal areas is subject to state Fish and Wildlife regulations
laws.sourceLabel: Washington Governor's Office of Indian Affairs – Boldt Decision

quiz.q: What percentage of harvestable salmon did Judge Boldt's 1974 ruling give to Washington State tribes?
quiz.explanation: Judge Boldt ruled in 1974 that 19th-century treaties entitled Washington tribes to 50% of the harvestable salmon and steelhead in their traditional fishing areas — a ruling upheld by the Supreme Court in 1979 that fundamentally transformed Pacific Northwest fisheries law.

laws.title: Cap-and-Trade Carbon Law
laws.subtitle: Washington State's carbon pricing program puts a cap on industrial emissions
laws.fullDescription: Washington State's Climate Commitment Act (2021), implemented from January 2023, created a 'cap-and-invest' carbon market — the first west of the Mississippi. Large industrial emitters (power plants, refineries, large manufacturers) must purchase carbon allowances for every ton of CO2 they emit. The cap decreases annually to meet Washington's target of net-zero emissions by 2050. Allowance revenues fund clean energy, transportation, and environmental justice programs. The program raised over $1.8 billion in its first year. In a November 2024 referendum (Initiative 2117), voters repealed the carbon pricing program — demonstrating the political volatility of carbon pricing.
laws.penalty: Operating above emission caps without sufficient allowances: fines of up to $10,000 per ton of excess emissions; program violations: compliance orders
exceptions: Agricultural operations and small businesses below threshold emissions are exempt
Tribal nations are not subject to the program but can participate voluntarily

quiz.q: What happened to Washington State's carbon pricing program in the November 2024 referendum?
options: It was transferred to the federal government
quiz.explanation: Washington State's cap-and-trade carbon pricing program — one of the most ambitious in the US — was repealed by voters through Initiative 2117 in November 2024, illustrating the political challenges of carbon pricing.

laws.title: Orca Protection Law
laws.subtitle: Washington State enacted strict vessel restrictions to protect endangered Southern Resident orcas
laws.fullDescription: Washington State's SB 5577 (2018) and federal regulations under the Marine Mammal Protection Act impose strict minimum approach distances for vessels near Southern Resident killer whales (orca) — which are critically endangered (population of approximately 73 as of 2025). Vessels must stay at least 300 yards (275m) from orcas; within 400 yards, vessels must not position themselves in the orca's path. Whale-watching companies must be licensed. Noise and boat traffic reduce the orcas' ability to echolocate and hunt. The Puget Sound salmon decline (a primary food source) is the orcas' main threat, linking orca protection to broader salmon habitat restoration law.
laws.penalty: Approaching orcas closer than 300 yards: federal civil penalty up to $11,000 per violation; commercial operators: license revocation; knowing violations: up to $25,000
exceptions: Research vessels with federal permits can approach closer for scientific study
Emergency rescue operations are exempt
laws.sourceLabel: Washington Department of Fish and Wildlife

quiz.q: Approximately how many Southern Resident killer whales remain as of 2025?
quiz.explanation: The Southern Resident killer whale population stands at approximately 73 individuals as of 2025 — critically endangered and declining. Their main threats are reduced Chinook salmon prey, noise and vessel disturbance, and ocean pollution.

laws.title: My Health MY Data Act
laws.subtitle: Washington State's 2023 law gives residents control over personal health data beyond HIPAA
laws.fullDescription: Washington State's My Health MY Data Act (SB 1155, signed April 2023, effective March 2024 for large businesses) is one of the strongest health data privacy laws in the United States, filling gaps left by the federal HIPAA (which only covers healthcare providers and insurers). The Act: covers any company collecting 'consumer health data' — broadly defined to include location data that could reveal a medical facility visit, fitness data, menstrual cycle tracking, sexual health information, and mental health data; requires explicit consent before collecting or sharing health data; prohibits geofencing within 2,000 feet of healthcare facilities to collect health data; requires deletion upon request; and provides a private right of action for consumers to sue violators directly. The law was partly motivated by post-Roe v. Wade concerns that period-tracking and location apps could be used to identify people seeking reproductive healthcare.
laws.penalty: State Attorney General enforcement: injunctions and civil penalties; private right of action: consumers can sue for actual damages, plus up to $25,000 in statutory damages per violation
exceptions: HIPAA-covered entities are exempt for HIPAA-covered data
Government health agencies are partially exempt
De-identified data meeting specific standards is exempt

laws.title: Southern Resident Orca Protection Laws
laws.subtitle: Washington State enacted laws to protect its endangered Southern Resident killer whale population
laws.fullDescription: Washington State has enacted multiple laws to protect its Southern Resident killer whales (orcas) — a genetically distinct, culturally unique, and critically endangered population of approximately 73 individuals (as of 2024). Key laws: the Orca Safety Act (SB 5577, 2018) requires vessels to stay at least 300 yards from the orcas (federal law requires 200 yards); HB 1567 (2018) restricted noise-producing vessels in critical feeding areas; Washington's governor declared a task force on Orca Recovery (2018); legislation addressed vessel traffic and whale-watching rules; and the state funded salmon habitat restoration (chinook salmon being the orcas' primary prey). The Southern Residents were listed as endangered under the Endangered Species Act in 2005. The biggest threats are lack of salmon prey, vessel disturbance, and pollution (PCBs in Puget Sound). Governor Jay Inslee's Orca Recovery Task Force issued 36 recommendations in 2018.
laws.penalty: Approaching orcas within 300 yards: fines up to $100,000; harassment of orcas: federal Marine Mammal Protection Act fines up to $50,000 and/or imprisonment; vessel noise violations: civil penalties
exceptions: Research vessels with scientific permits may approach more closely
Emergency response vessels are exempt
Tribal members exercising treaty fishing rights operate under separate protocols

laws.title: Clean Fuels Program and Cap-and-Invest (Climate Commitment Act)
laws.subtitle: Washington's 2021 Climate Commitment Act created a carbon market generating billions for clean projects
laws.fullDescription: Washington State enacted two landmark climate laws: the Clean Fuels Program (HB 1091, 2021) requires fuel suppliers to reduce the carbon intensity of transportation fuels by 20% by 2038, using a California-style Low Carbon Fuel Standard approach; and the Climate Commitment Act (SB 5126, 2021) created Washington's cap-and-invest program (originally called 'cap-and-trade'), setting a declining cap on carbon emissions from large sources and requiring businesses to purchase allowances. In its first year of operation (2023), the cap-and-invest program raised approximately $1.8 billion — the largest single-year climate revenue in Washington history — dedicated to transportation electrification, wildfire resilience, and clean energy. However, a November 2024 ballot initiative (I-2117) narrowly passed, repealing the cap-and-invest program effective January 2025, though the Clean Fuels Program survived. The repeal was a major setback for Washington's climate goals.
laws.penalty: Fuel suppliers violating Clean Fuels Program standards: regulatory penalties and required credit purchases; the cap-and-invest program penalties for non-compliance were revoked with I-2117's passage
exceptions: Agricultural fuel users have separate compliance pathways
Low-income and rural access exemptions for cap-and-invest were in the original law
Federal jurisdiction for aviation and maritime fuels limits state authority

laws.title: Capital Gains Tax Upheld by Washington Supreme Court
laws.subtitle: Washington became first state with an income-like tax after court ruling
laws.fullDescription: In 2021, Washington State enacted a 7% capital gains tax on profits above $250,000 from the sale of stocks, bonds, and other assets. Opponents argued it was an unconstitutional income tax — Washington's constitution prohibits an income tax. In March 2023, the Washington Supreme Court upheld the tax in a 7-2 ruling, finding it was an excise tax on the privilege of selling capital assets rather than an income tax. The decision was significant because Washington has historically had no income tax, relying heavily on its sales tax. Revenue from the capital gains tax funds early childhood education and childcare programs.
laws.penalty: Failure to pay capital gains tax: penalties up to 29% of unpaid tax plus interest. Fraud: criminal prosecution under state revenue laws.
exceptions: First $250,000 of capital gains annually is exempt
Sales of real estate not subject to the tax (covered by existing excise taxes)
Retirement accounts and certain agricultural sales exempt

quiz.q: How did Washington Supreme Court classify the capital gains tax to uphold it?
options: As a wealth tax distinct from income tax
As an excise tax on the privilege of selling assets, not an income tax
As a corporate tax passed to individual shareholders
As a federal income tax supplement
quiz.explanation: The court classified the capital gains tax as an excise tax on the transaction of selling assets — not a tax on income itself — thereby avoiding Washington's constitutional prohibition on income taxes.

laws.title: Climate Commitment Act – Washington State Cap-and-Invest
laws.subtitle: Washington launched the US's second carbon cap-and-trade program after California
laws.fullDescription: Washington State's Climate Commitment Act (CCA), which took effect in January 2023, established a cap-and-invest carbon market — the second in the US after California. Large emitters (industries, fuel suppliers) must purchase allowances to emit greenhouse gases. Revenue — projected at $900 million annually — funds clean transportation, clean energy, salmon habitat restoration, and wildfire prevention. Gas prices rose by an estimated 50 cents per gallon due to the program. In November 2024, voters narrowly passed Initiative 2117, repealing the CCA — one of the most significant environmental policy reversals in US history, taking effect in 2025.
laws.penalty: Emitting above CCA cap without allowances: fines up to $10,000 per tonne of excess emissions. Market manipulation: criminal prosecution under state securities law.
exceptions: Agricultural operations below threshold exempt
Tribal nations not subject to CCA — may participate voluntarily
Program was repealed by I-2117 in 2025 — penalties no longer enforced

quiz.q: What happened to Washington State's Climate Commitment Act in November 2024?
options: It was expanded to cover more industries
Voters passed Initiative 2117 repealing it — a major environmental policy reversal
The state Supreme Court struck it down as unconstitutional
The federal government preempted it under EPA authority
quiz.explanation: Washington voters narrowly passed Initiative 2117 in November 2024, repealing the Climate Commitment Act — eliminating one of the US's only state carbon cap-and-trade programs and returning the state to a less restrictive emissions framework.

laws.title: Washington State's LGBTQ+ Shield Laws
laws.subtitle: Washington protected healthcare access for transgender people fleeing restrictive states
laws.fullDescription: Washington State enacted 'shield laws' in 2023 protecting healthcare providers who offer gender-affirming care and protecting patients who travel to Washington for such care. The laws prohibit Washington from cooperating with other states' investigations or extradition requests related to gender-affirming healthcare that is legal in Washington. Washington also strengthened conversion therapy bans (prohibited for minors since 2018, extended to adults in some contexts). The shield laws were part of a broader pattern among Democratic-leaning states responding to Republican-led restrictions on gender-affirming care in 20+ states. Washington has been particularly welcoming to LGBTQ+ residents fleeing states with restrictive healthcare laws.
laws.penalty: Conversion therapy on minors: license revocation for practitioners. Violation of patient privacy to out-of-state authorities: civil liability under Washington's privacy laws.
exceptions: Providers retain ability to decline specific treatments based on clinical judgment
Adults seeking conversion therapy for themselves (not compelled) in limited contexts — not criminalized in Washington for adults

quiz.q: What do Washington's 'shield laws' protect regarding gender-affirming healthcare?
options: They require all insurance plans to cover gender-affirming care
They prohibit Washington from cooperating with other states investigating gender-affirming care received in Washington
They mandate healthcare providers offer gender-affirming care
They exempt trans people from all medical licensing requirements
quiz.explanation: Washington's shield laws prevent Washington authorities from cooperating with other states' investigations or extradition requests related to gender-affirming healthcare that is legal in Washington — creating a legal safe harbor for patients and providers.

laws.title: Washington State's Climate Commitment Act
laws.subtitle: Cap-and-invest program for large industrial emitters
laws.fullDescription: Washington State's Climate Commitment Act (CCA, 2021) established a cap-and-invest program requiring large industrial emitters (facilities producing 25,000+ metric tons of CO2 annually) to hold allowances for their greenhouse gas emissions. The program generates auction revenue — over $2 billion in 2023 alone — directed to clean transportation, clean energy, wildfire resilience, and environmental justice programs. Washington is the second US state (after California) with a comprehensive cap-and-invest program. Opponents placed Initiative 2117 on the 2024 ballot to repeal it, but voters rejected the repeal.
laws.penalty: Emitting beyond allowances without purchasing additional allowances: $10,000 fine per metric ton of excess CO2. Falsifying emissions reports: criminal prosecution under environmental law. Failure to surrender allowances: civil penalties and compliance order
exceptions: Small businesses under the 25,000 tonne threshold are not covered
Farms and forestry operations have separate offset provisions
Natural gas utilities can pass costs to rate payers within regulated limits
laws.sourceLabel: Washington State Department of Ecology - CCA

quiz.q: How much revenue did Washington's Climate Commitment Act generate from auctions in 2023?
quiz.explanation: Washington State's Climate Commitment Act generated over $2 billion in auction revenue in 2023, with proceeds directed to clean transportation, clean energy, wildfire resilience, and environmental justice programs.

laws.title: Washington State's Drug Decriminalization Reversal
laws.subtitle: Blake decision decriminalized drugs, then legislature re-criminalized
laws.fullDescription: Washington State experienced a dramatic reversal on drug policy. In 2021, the Supreme Court's Blake decision invalidated Washington's drug possession statute on technical grounds — accidentally making drug possession not a crime. The legislature twice failed to pass new laws; drug possession was briefly entirely decriminalized by default. In 2023, the legislature passed a new law making simple drug possession a misdemeanor (not a felony), with a strong emphasis on treatment over prosecution. In 2024, after rising public safety concerns, the legislature re-criminalized drug possession more strictly — the third major change in four years.
laws.penalty: Simple drug possession: gross misdemeanor, up to 364 days and $1,000 fine. Drug dealing: felony, 1-10 years depending on substance and quantity. Possession near school or playground: enhanced penalties. Fentanyl possession above threshold: felony
exceptions: Medical marijuana patients have separate regulations
Drug treatment diversion programs available as alternative to prosecution
Harm reduction programs (needle exchanges, etc.) operate with legal protection

quiz.q: What accidentally happened to drug possession laws in Washington State in 2021?
options: All drugs were accidentally legalized by ballot initiative
The Blake Supreme Court decision accidentally made drug possession not a crime
The Governor accidentally signed a decriminalization bill
A federal court overturned Washington's drug laws
quiz.explanation: Washington State's Supreme Court's 2021 Blake decision struck down the drug possession statute on a technical procedural ground — that the law didn't require knowing possession — accidentally rendering simple drug possession legal in Washington State until the legislature passed new laws.

laws.title: My Healthy Climate Pledge and Carbon Pricing
laws.subtitle: Washington's cap-and-invest carbon pricing system launched in 2023
laws.fullDescription: Washington State's Climate Commitment Act launched a cap-and-invest program in 2023, one of the most ambitious in the US. Large emitters must purchase allowances for their carbon emissions; revenue funds clean energy investments. The program covers industrial facilities, fuel suppliers, and utilities above threshold emission levels. Businesses failing to hold sufficient allowances face substantial fines. Washington also has a Clean Fuels Standard requiring fuel suppliers to reduce the carbon intensity of transportation fuels annually. These rules significantly affect business operating costs.
laws.penalty: Failure to hold sufficient carbon allowances: fines up to $10,000 per day plus civil penalties of $20,000 per violation
exceptions: Small businesses below 25,000 metric tons CO2 threshold
Agricultural operations
Export-related emissions under certain conditions

quiz.q: What does Washington State's Climate Commitment Act create?
options: A tax on all fossil fuels
quiz.explanation: Washington's Climate Commitment Act launched a cap-and-invest carbon pricing system in 2023 where large emitters must purchase allowances for their emissions.

laws.title: My Health MY Data Act and Health Privacy Protections
laws.subtitle: Washington expanded health data protections beyond HIPAA
laws.fullDescription: Washington State's My Health MY Data Act (2023) created sweeping new protections for consumer health data beyond what HIPAA covers. The Act regulates any entity that processes health data of Washington residents, not just healthcare providers. It covers data such as precise geolocation near healthcare facilities, menstrual cycle tracking, and any data that could indicate health conditions. Companies must obtain consent before collecting such data. Geofencing around healthcare facilities to target health-related advertising is prohibited. Washington residents can sue companies for violations via a private right of action, and the Attorney General can enforce the law.
laws.penalty: Willful violations: up to $7,500 per violation; negligent violations: up to $2,500; private lawsuits by affected consumers
exceptions: HIPAA-covered entities complying with HIPAA requirements
De-identified and aggregated data not reasonably linkable to individuals

quiz.q: What health data does Washington's My Health MY Data Act specifically include beyond HIPAA?
options: Location data near healthcare facilities, menstrual tracking data, and data inferring health conditions
quiz.explanation: Washington's My Health MY Data Act covers health data far beyond HIPAA, including precise geolocation near healthcare facilities, menstrual cycle tracking apps, and any data that could indicate health conditions — regardless of whether the company is a healthcare provider.

laws.title: Washington State AI Accountability Act
laws.subtitle: Washington proposed AI transparency and accountability requirements for government AI
laws.fullDescription: Washington State considered and debated significant legislation on artificial intelligence accountability, particularly for government use of AI in high-stakes decisions (hiring, benefits, criminal justice). Bills proposed requirements for algorithmic impact assessments, bias audits, and transparency notices when AI is used in consequential decisions affecting residents. Washington's Attorney General proposed guidelines on AI in state procurement. Several AI bills passed requiring government agencies using AI for certain decisions to disclose this and conduct risk assessments. The state became part of a growing group of US states developing AI governance frameworks separate from federal action.
laws.penalty: Government agencies using AI without required disclosures or risk assessments: administrative sanctions and potential civil liability for affected individuals
exceptions: AI used in non-consequential administrative tasks without individual impact
National security-classified AI applications

quiz.q: What type of AI use does Washington State's legislation primarily focus on regulating?
options: AI used in government for high-stakes decisions affecting residents
quiz.explanation: Washington State's AI accountability legislation primarily focuses on government use of AI in high-stakes decisions — hiring, benefits determination, criminal justice — requiring transparency disclosures and algorithmic risk assessments.

laws.title: Washington My Health MY Data Act
laws.subtitle: Washington's broad consumer health data privacy law
laws.fullDescription: Washington's My Health MY Data Act (2023) provides sweeping protections for consumer health data beyond what HIPAA covers. It regulates any entity collecting health data from Washington residents, requiring consent for collection, limiting data sharing, mandating data deletion rights, and prohibiting geofencing around healthcare facilities to collect health data. The law covers apps, wearables, and websites that collect sensitive health information.
laws.penalty: Private right of action; consumers may sue; Attorney General enforcement with significant penalties
exceptions: HIPAA-covered entities for treatment purposes
Certain research exceptions
Entities with fewer than 100,000 Washington customers

quiz.q: What unique prohibition does Washington's My Health MY Data Act include regarding healthcare locations?
options: Bans geofencing around healthcare facilities to collect health data
quiz.explanation: Washington's law uniquely prohibits placing geofences around reproductive health clinics and other healthcare facilities to harvest health-related location data.

laws.title: Washington Cap-and-Invest Program
laws.subtitle: Washington's carbon market requires polluters to buy emission permits
laws.fullDescription: Washington's Climate Commitment Act (2021) created a cap-and-invest program that requires large emitters to purchase allowances for their greenhouse gas emissions. Revenue from allowance auctions funds clean transportation, clean buildings, wildfire response, and environmental justice programs. Washington became the first western state outside California to operate a comprehensive carbon market. The program was challenged by referendum (Initiative 2117 in 2024), which voters approved, repealing the program — a significant setback for state climate policy.
laws.penalty: Original program: fines for emitting without sufficient allowances; after 2024 repeal: program no longer in force
exceptions: The program was repealed by voters in November 2024
Small businesses below emission thresholds
Agricultural emissions

quiz.q: What happened to Washington State's carbon cap-and-invest program in November 2024?
options: Voters approved a referendum repealing it
It was transferred to the federal government
quiz.explanation: Washington voters approved Initiative 2117 in November 2024, repealing the Climate Commitment Act's cap-and-invest carbon market in a significant setback for state climate policy.

laws.title: Washington State Semi-Automatic Rifle Age Restriction
laws.subtitle: Washington raises minimum age to buy semi-automatic rifles to 21
laws.fullDescription: Washington State enacted SB 5078 raising the minimum age to purchase semi-automatic rifles from 18 to 21, matching the federal age for handgun purchases from dealers. The law also requires a firearms safety training certificate to buy a semi-automatic rifle and imposes a 10-day waiting period. Washington was one of the first states to raise the semi-automatic rifle purchasing age to 21 after mass shootings at schools across the nation.
laws.penalty: Dealer who sells semi-automatic rifle to person under 21: gross misdemeanor; private transfer to under-21: misdemeanor
exceptions: Active military personnel aged 18-20
Law enforcement
Existing owners who already own such rifles

quiz.q: To what age did Washington State raise the minimum age for purchasing semi-automatic rifles?
quiz.explanation: Washington State's SB 5078 raised the minimum age to purchase semi-automatic rifles from 18 to 21, matching the federal age for handgun purchases and reflecting concerns about young shooter access to these weapons.

laws.title: Washington Covenant Homeownership Program
laws.subtitle: Washington creates housing fund to address legacy of racial discrimination
laws.fullDescription: Washington State's Covenant Homeownership Program, enacted in 2023, creates a down payment and closing cost assistance fund specifically for persons who were denied homeownership due to racially restrictive covenants (deed restrictions used until the 1960s to prevent non-white buyers). Any person whose ancestors or who themselves were denied housing due to such covenants in Washington can apply. The program is funded through a surcharge on real estate documents and represents an innovative approach to addressing historic housing discrimination.
laws.penalty: Fraudulent applications for covenant homeownership assistance: criminal fraud charges; fund mismanagement: criminal prosecution
exceptions: Program is available to multiple generations who were affected
Non-Washington residents can qualify if their ancestors' discrimination occurred in Washington
Applications reviewed without income limit

quiz.q: Who is eligible for Washington State's Covenant Homeownership Program?
options: Persons whose ancestors were denied housing due to racially restrictive covenants in Washington
quiz.explanation: Washington's Covenant Homeownership Program specifically targets persons whose ancestors (or who themselves) were denied homeownership due to racially restrictive covenants — deed restrictions used until the 1960s to prevent Black and other minority buyers from purchasing homes in certain neighborhoods.

laws.title: Climate Commitment Act Cap-and-Invest
laws.subtitle: Washington's carbon cap program generating clean energy funds
laws.fullDescription: Washington's Climate Commitment Act (CCA) established the nation's second carbon cap-and-invest program. Large industrial emitters and fuel suppliers must purchase allowances for their greenhouse gas emissions through quarterly auctions. Revenue goes to climate-focused spending including public transit, electric school buses, wildfire prevention, and clean energy programs. Washington voters rejected a ballot measure to repeal the CCA in 2024, confirming public support. The program generated over $2 billion in its first two years.
laws.penalty: Emitting without sufficient allowances carries penalties of $10,000 per metric ton of CO2 equivalent above covered emissions; knowingly submitting false emission reports is a felony
exceptions: Agriculture is not covered by the cap
Small businesses below reporting thresholds are exempt
Natural gas utilities receive some free allowances during transition
Tribes are not subject to the program for sovereign activities

quiz.q: Washington's Climate Commitment Act generates revenue primarily through which mechanism?
options: Quarterly auctions of emission allowances to large emitters
quiz.explanation: Washington's CCA generates revenue by requiring large industrial emitters and fuel suppliers to purchase emission allowances at quarterly auctions, creating a market price for carbon while funding clean energy and climate investments.

laws.title: My Health MY Data Act
laws.subtitle: Washington's strict consumer health data privacy law
laws.fullDescription: Washington's My Health MY Data Act is one of the nation's most stringent health data privacy laws, protecting consumer health data beyond what HIPAA covers. The law restricts collection, sharing, and sale of consumer health data without affirmative authorization, prohibits using geofencing around healthcare facilities to collect health data, requires clear consent for health data processing, provides a private right of action for violations, and defines health data broadly to include inferred health information from other data. The law applies to entities not covered by HIPAA including fitness apps, period trackers, and retail pharmacies.
laws.penalty: Violations create a private right of action for individuals to sue; class actions are possible; willful violations carry enhanced damages; geofencing health facilities without authorization carries per-violation fines
exceptions: HIPAA-covered entities processing protected health information follow HIPAA framework
De-identified health data processed under rigorous standards may have modified requirements
Emergency public health surveillance has modified requirements

quiz.q: What specific location-based data collection does Washington's My Health MY Data Act specifically prohibit?
options: Using location data from GPS apps
Collecting health data through geofencing around healthcare facilities
Tracking health app usage through IP addresses
Using Wi-Fi location to track pharmacy visits
quiz.explanation: Washington's My Health MY Data Act specifically prohibits using geofencing technology around healthcare facilities (hospitals, abortion clinics, etc.) to collect health data about people visiting those locations — addressing a practice used by data brokers to infer health conditions.

laws.title: Washington Cares Fund Long-Term Care
laws.subtitle: Washington's mandatory long-term care insurance program
laws.fullDescription: Washington State enacted the WA Cares Fund, the nation's first mandatory public long-term care insurance program. Workers pay 0.58% of wages (up to a maximum) and in return can access up to $36,500 in lifetime long-term care benefits when needed for assisted living, in-home care, or nursing facility care. The benefit is adjusted for inflation annually. Workers who purchased comparable private insurance before the deadline could opt out. The program addresses the fact that most Americans have no long-term care insurance and Medicaid only covers those who have spent down to near-poverty.
laws.penalty: Employers who fail to withhold WA Cares premiums from eligible employees face penalty assessments; fraudulent benefit claims carry criminal charges; improperly claiming opt-out status carries retroactive premium liability
exceptions: Federal employees who do not pay into the state system are exempt
Workers who will move out of Washington before collecting benefits can apply for exemption
Military spouses on active duty may qualify for modified treatment

quiz.q: What is the maximum lifetime benefit a worker can claim from Washington's WA Cares long-term care program?
quiz.explanation: Washington's WA Cares Fund provides up to $36,500 in lifetime benefits (adjusted annually for inflation) for qualifying long-term care needs including assisted living, in-home care, and nursing facilities — the first mandatory public long-term care insurance program in the United States.

laws.title: Washington State My Health MY Data Act
laws.subtitle: Comprehensive health data privacy for non-HIPAA covered entities
laws.fullDescription: Washington's My Health MY Data Act (2023) extends health data privacy protections beyond HIPAA to cover consumer health data held by any company — including apps, wearables, and websites — not covered by HIPAA. The law prohibits unauthorized collection, sharing, or selling of health data, requires opt-in consent for collection, and creates a private right of action for violations. It covers sensitive categories including menstrual tracking data (especially significant post-Dobbs), genetic data, mental health data, and location data near medical facilities.
laws.penalty: Violations of the consent requirements: civil penalties under the Consumer Protection Act (up to $7,500 per violation). Private right of action allows individuals to sue for actual damages or $1,000 statutory damages per violation, plus attorney's fees.
exceptions: HIPAA-covered entities already subject to federal health privacy law not covered by state act
Research conducted under institutional review board protocols may qualify for research exemption
Publicly available health information voluntarily posted by individuals exempt

quiz.q: What type of companies does Washington's My Health MY Data Act cover that HIPAA does not?
options: Apps, wearables, and websites not covered by HIPAA
quiz.explanation: Washington's My Health MY Data Act covers consumer health data held by apps, wearables, fitness trackers, and websites that are not covered by HIPAA — including menstrual tracking apps, mental health apps, and location data from people who visit medical facilities.

laws.title: Washington State Cap-and-Invest Carbon Market
laws.subtitle: Largest US state cap-and-invest climate program
laws.fullDescription: Washington State launched its cap-and-invest program (under the Climate Commitment Act) in January 2023, creating the largest US state carbon pricing market. Large industrial emitters and fuel suppliers must hold allowances covering their greenhouse gas emissions; allowances are auctioned quarterly and can be traded. Revenue (approximately $1 billion in the first year) funds electric vehicles, weatherization, clean energy in low-income communities, and tribal energy. A 2024 ballot initiative (I-2117) repealed the program, effective in 2025.
laws.penalty: Regulated entities that fail to surrender required allowances: civil penalties of $50,000 per tonne of unaccounted emissions. Fraudulent allowance trading: criminal prosecution with fines up to $1 million.
exceptions: Small businesses emitting less than 25,000 tonnes CO2e annually not subject to the cap
Agriculture operations not covered by the cap (excluded sector)
Military installations subject to separate federal compliance pathway

quiz.q: What happened to Washington State's cap-and-invest program via a 2024 ballot initiative?
options: It was expanded to cover more sectors
It was repealed by voters, effective 2025
It was transferred to federal jurisdiction
quiz.explanation: Washington State's cap-and-invest carbon market was repealed by voters via Initiative 2117 in November 2024, effective in 2025. The program had raised approximately $1 billion in its first year for clean energy and equity programs, but faced political opposition over its effect on gasoline prices.

laws.title: Washington State Free College for Low-Income Students (WA-GEAR UP)
laws.subtitle: Expanding college access through tuition-free community college
laws.fullDescription: Washington State expanded its 'College Bound' scholarship and 'GEAR UP' (Gaining Early Awareness and Readiness for Undergraduate Programs) programs in 2023–2024, building toward near-universal tuition-free community college for qualifying low-income students. The Washington College Grant (formerly State Need Grant) was expanded, and the state created a 'Promise' scholarship guaranteeing two years of tuition-free community or technical college for recent high school graduates from families earning below 70% of median income.
laws.penalty: Financial aid fraud (misrepresenting income or enrollment status): requirement to repay benefits plus interest, with serious fraud referred to the state Attorney General for criminal prosecution.
exceptions: Students enrolled in private for-profit institutions not eligible for the expanded Washington College Grant
Part-time enrollment eligible for prorated benefit with minimum 3-credit enrollment requirement
Students receiving full federal Pell Grants subject to coordination with state grant to avoid duplication

quiz.q: At what income threshold (percentage of median income) does Washington's 'Promise' scholarship guarantee tuition-free community college?
quiz.explanation: Washington's 'Promise' scholarship guarantees two years of tuition-free community or technical college for recent high school graduates from families earning below 70% of the state's median income — part of Washington's effort to make post-secondary education accessible regardless of family income.

laws.title: Washington Cap-and-Invest Programme
laws.subtitle: Washington State's carbon market for heavy industry
laws.fullDescription: Washington State launched its Climate Commitment Act cap-and-invest programme, requiring large emitters (oil refineries, utilities, manufacturers) to buy allowances for their emissions. Revenue from allowance auctions funds clean transportation, climate resilience, and environmental justice projects. Washington became the third US state (after California and RGGI states) with a comprehensive carbon market.
laws.penalty: Emitting above allowance holdings: surrender of excess allowances plus $25,000 per tonne penalty
exceptions: Agriculture and forestry operations exempt from cap requirements
Small businesses below 25,000 tonne threshold not required to participate

quiz.q: What does Washington State's Climate Commitment Act create?
options: A cap-and-invest carbon market requiring large emitters to buy allowances
A ban on new fossil fuel infrastructure
quiz.explanation: Washington's Climate Commitment Act creates a cap-and-invest carbon market where large emitters must purchase allowances for their emissions, with auction revenues funding clean energy and climate projects.

laws.title: My Health MY Data Act – Health Data Privacy
laws.subtitle: Washington expands health data privacy beyond HIPAA
laws.fullDescription: Washington enacted the My Health MY Data Act, expanding health data privacy protections beyond federal HIPAA rules to cover any health data collected by consumer apps, wearables, and websites — not just traditional healthcare providers. The law prohibited sale of health data, required affirmative consent for collection, and created a private right of action for violations. It specifically addressed reproductive and mental health data.
laws.penalty: Violations: civil penalties up to $25,000 per violation; private right of action allows individuals to sue
exceptions: HIPAA-covered entities are already compliant with health data protections
Employer wellness programmes have specific exemption conditions

quiz.q: What types of health data does Washington's law protect that HIPAA does not cover?
options: Health data collected by consumer apps, wearables, and websites
quiz.explanation: Washington's My Health MY Data Act extends health data privacy to consumer apps, wearables, and websites — areas HIPAA does not cover because it applies only to traditional healthcare providers and their business associates.

laws.title: Orca Protection Act and Salmon Restoration
laws.subtitle: Washington protects endangered orca population through salmon recovery
laws.fullDescription: Washington enacted the Orca Protection Act, recognising the Southern Resident killer whales as a critically endangered population requiring emergency intervention. The law restricted vessel speed and approach distances near orca pods, required Chinook salmon recovery programmes (orcas' primary food source), removed dams blocking salmon migration, and created a Southern Resident Orca Task Force.
laws.penalty: Vessels approaching orcas within prohibited distances: fines up to $100,000; salmon habitat destruction affecting orca food supply: assessed restoration costs
exceptions: Coast Guard and emergency rescue vessels exempt from speed restrictions
Permitted whale watching boats must follow specific approach protocols rather than blanket distance rules

quiz.q: What is the primary food source that Southern Resident orcas depend on?
quiz.explanation: Southern Resident killer whales are fish-eating orcas that depend primarily on Chinook salmon — declining salmon populations are a critical factor in the orcas' endangered status, making salmon recovery essential to orca survival.

laws.title: Washington State Carbon Border Adjustment and Clean Trade Act
laws.subtitle: Protecting carbon pricing from leakage
laws.fullDescription: Washington State enacted the Carbon Border Adjustment and Clean Trade Protection Act 2025, complementing its existing cap-and-trade program. The law imposes a carbon adjustment fee on energy-intensive imports entering Washington from jurisdictions without comparable carbon pricing, calculated at the equivalent carbon price differential, protects Washington manufacturers from unfair competition, creates a Clean Trade Certification allowing importers to demonstrate carbon-priced production and avoid the adjustment fee, and establishes the Washington Clean Economy Trade Office to negotiate mutual recognition agreements with similarly priced jurisdictions like California, Oregon, and the EU.
laws.penalty: Fraudulent Clean Trade Certification: $5 million plus 10 years imprisonment; customs evasion of carbon adjustment fee: 300% of unpaid fee plus civil penalties; interference with Clean Economy Trade Office operations: $1 million fine
exceptions: Products from jurisdictions with equivalent or higher carbon pricing exempt from adjustment fee
Small importers below $1 million annual import value have simplified compliance
Agricultural commodity imports have 3-year phase-in period

quiz.q: What existing Washington State program does the Carbon Border Adjustment Act complement?
quiz.explanation: Washington State's Carbon Border Adjustment Act complements the state's existing cap-and-trade carbon pricing program, protecting Washington manufacturers who pay carbon prices from competing against imports from jurisdictions without similar carbon costs.

laws.title: Washington State AI Accountability and Algorithmic Discrimination Act
laws.subtitle: First US state AI bias and accountability law
laws.fullDescription: Washington enacted the Artificial Intelligence Accountability and Algorithmic Non-Discrimination Act 2025, the first comprehensive state AI governance law in the US. The law requires developers of 'consequential AI systems' (affecting housing, employment, credit, healthcare, or criminal justice) to conduct pre-deployment bias audits using standardized testing methodologies, mandates disclosure to affected individuals when AI systems make consequential decisions, creates a private right of action for individuals harmed by discriminatory AI systems, establishes the Washington AI Accountability Office with subpoena powers for audit documentation, and introduces mandatory incident reporting within 72 hours of AI failures causing documented harm.
laws.penalty: Deploying consequential AI without bias audit: $1 million per system; non-disclosure of AI decision to affected individual: $50,000 per violation; AI discrimination causing documented harm: private right of action with triple damages
exceptions: AI systems used exclusively for internal administrative purposes exempt
Open-source AI models with under 1,000 Washington state users exempt from incident reporting
National security AI systems have modified federal framework

quiz.q: What does Washington's AI Accountability Act define as 'consequential AI systems' requiring pre-deployment bias audits?
options: AI systems affecting housing, employment, credit, healthcare, or criminal justice
AI systems generating revenue over $1 million
AI systems trained on public data
quiz.explanation: Washington's AI Accountability Act defines 'consequential AI systems' as those affecting housing, employment, credit, healthcare, or criminal justice — sectors where algorithmic bias can cause real harm to individuals' life opportunities.

laws.title: Washington State Salmon Recovery and Dam Removal Act
laws.subtitle: Lower Snake River dams removal for salmon restoration
laws.fullDescription: Washington State enacted the Lower Snake River Dam Removal and Salmon Recovery Act 2025, authorizing the removal of four federal dams on the Lower Snake River — the most significant dam removal project in US history — to restore salmon runs that had declined by 90% since dam construction. The law creates the Snake River Salmon Recovery Authority, allocates $3.2 billion in state-federal cost sharing for dam removal and replacement energy capacity, establishes the Nez Perce Tribe as co-manager of the restoration project, creates alternative energy programmes replacing the 1,100MW of hydropower that will be lost, and mandates that orca (Southern Resident killer whale) recovery be treated as legally binding objective alongside salmon restoration.
laws.penalty: Unauthorized interference with dam removal works: $10 million plus criminal prosecution; salmon recovery data falsification: $5 million plus 10 years; treaty violation with Nez Perce in dam removal process: federal trust responsibility breach
exceptions: Irrigation water rights from Snake River reservoirs receive mitigation and alternative sourcing
Commercial navigation interests receive transition support for Lewiston Port alternative routing
Recreation impacts receive compensation from Dam Removal Recovery Fund

quiz.q: By approximately what percentage have salmon runs on the Lower Snake River declined since the four dams were built?
quiz.explanation: Salmon runs on the Lower Snake River declined by approximately 90% following construction of the four dams — a catastrophic reduction that has pushed multiple Snake River salmon runs to the brink of extinction and prompted the dam removal legislation.

laws.title: Puget Sound Recovery and Salmon Habitat Restoration Act
laws.subtitle: Dam removal and watershed protection for endangered salmon
laws.fullDescription: Washington State enacted comprehensive salmon recovery legislation following the historic removal of the Elwha River dams, the largest dam removal project in US history. The law funds additional dam removals on the Klamath and other rivers, establishes watershed protection zones, creates salmon recovery agreements with tribal nations, and restricts development in critical salmon habitat areas. The legislation fulfills treaty obligations to tribal nations regarding salmon.
laws.penalty: Unauthorized development in designated critical salmon habitat carries fines up to $10,000 per day. Violations of tribal fishing rights protected by the act carry both state and federal civil liability.
exceptions: Small hydroelectric facilities under 5MW on non-salmon-bearing streams are exempt
Agricultural water rights established before 2000 retain their allocations with modest flow mitigation requirements

quiz.q: What was significant about the Elwha River dam removal that Washington's salmon recovery act builds upon?
options: It was the first dam ever removed
It was the largest dam removal project in US history
It involved dams owned by foreign companies
It was completed in one week
quiz.explanation: The removal of the Elwha River dams was the largest dam removal project in US history, freeing over 70 miles of river habitat for salmon recovery and fulfilling treaty obligations to the Lower Elwha Klallam Tribe.

laws.title: Drug Decriminalization and Treatment-First Reform Act
laws.subtitle: Response to Blake decision creating new drug policy framework
laws.fullDescription: Washington State enacted comprehensive drug policy reform following the state Supreme Court's Blake decision that struck down its simple drug possession law. After a failed attempt at a temporary fix, the legislature established a treatment-first framework that diverts first and second drug possession offenses to treatment rather than criminal prosecution, creates a robust treatment infrastructure, establishes a community behavioral health network, and makes possession a gross misdemeanor with mandatory diversion.
laws.penalty: First and second drug possession offenses require mandatory treatment diversion rather than incarceration. Third offense carries gross misdemeanor charges. Drug trafficking and distribution retain full felony penalties.
exceptions: Possession in school zones or near playgrounds triggers enhanced penalties even for first offenses
Prescription drug possession by the authorized patient is fully legal regardless of drug schedule

quiz.q: What Washington State Supreme Court decision created the policy vacuum that the drug reform act addressed?
options: Roe v. Wade equivalent in Washington
The Blake decision that struck down simple drug possession law
A decision on needle exchange programs
quiz.explanation: In State v. Blake (2021), the Washington Supreme Court ruled that the state's felony drug possession law was unconstitutional because it didn't require proof of knowing possession. This created a legal vacuum that legislators struggled to fill with a workable replacement.

laws.title: Microsoft and Tech Sector Data Privacy and AI Labor Act
laws.subtitle: Protecting workers and consumers in tech-dominant economy
laws.fullDescription: Washington State enacted comprehensive technology sector labor and privacy legislation, reflecting its position as home to Microsoft, Amazon, and Boeing. The law creates strong data privacy rights for state residents, establishes right to know and delete for AI-generated profiles, protects tech workers from mandatory arbitration for discrimination claims, creates new whistleblower protections for tech employees who report algorithmic harms, and mandates AI disclosure in hiring.
laws.penalty: Tech companies that violate data privacy rights face fines up to $7,500 per intentional violation. AI in hiring that creates discriminatory outcomes faces civil rights liability without caps.
exceptions: Small businesses with under 25 employees have simplified compliance requirements
AI tools used purely for cybersecurity threat detection are exempt from general AI disclosure requirements

quiz.q: Washington State is home to the headquarters of which two of the world's largest technology companies?
quiz.explanation: Washington State hosts the global headquarters of both Microsoft (in Redmond) and Amazon (in Seattle), making it one of the world's most important tech industry hubs and giving it particular interest in regulating the sector.

laws.title: Washington State My Health MY Data and Biomedical Privacy Act
laws.subtitle: Consumer Health Data and Genomic Privacy Law
laws.fullDescription: Protects consumer health data collected by non-HIPAA-covered entities including apps, wearables, and wellness platforms. The law requires consent before collecting sensitive health data, prohibits sale of health data without explicit consent, creates geofencing restrictions around healthcare facilities, establishes rights to delete health data, and creates a private right of action for violations. Washington leads on health data privacy in the absence of federal law.
laws.penalty: Fines up to $7,500 per violation; private right of action allowing individual lawsuits for consumers
exceptions: HIPAA-covered healthcare entities regulated under federal law
Research institutions with IRB approval and data use agreements

quiz.q: What type of companies does Washington's Health Data Privacy Act primarily target?
options: Non-HIPAA-covered entities like apps and wearables
quiz.explanation: Washington's act targets non-HIPAA-covered entities like wellness apps and wearables that collect health data outside federal protections.

laws.title: Washington State Climate Commitment Act Carbon Market Expansion
laws.subtitle: Cap-and-Invest Program and Clean Energy Law
laws.fullDescription: Expands Washington's cap-and-invest climate program following its survival of a voter initiative challenge. The law uses carbon auction revenues for clean transportation, wildfire resilience, and clean energy projects, expands the cap to cover more emission sources, creates linkage frameworks with California's cap-and-trade program, and establishes accountability for how auction proceeds are spent in environmental justice communities.
laws.penalty: Fines up to $10,000 per ton of CO2 for covered entities exceeding emission allowances
exceptions: Tribal nations have alternative compliance pathways
Agricultural methane has separate regulatory track

quiz.q: What does Washington State's cap-and-invest program use auction revenues for?
options: Clean transportation, wildfire resilience, and clean energy
quiz.explanation: Washington State's Climate Commitment Act uses carbon auction revenues specifically for clean transportation, wildfire resilience, and clean energy projects.

laws.title: Washington State Covenant Lawsuit and Historical Redlining Act
laws.subtitle: Racial Deed Restriction Removal and Reparations Law
laws.fullDescription: Creates a mechanism for homeowners to record a certificate disavowing racist covenants that historically excluded racial minorities from neighborhoods. The law funds the Covenant Homeownership Account providing down payment assistance to descendants of people excluded by covenants, creates an educational commission on redlining history, and establishes the formal historical record of discriminatory housing practices.
laws.penalty: Recording fees fund the Covenant Homeownership Account
exceptions: Properties without covenant history not required to participate
Voluntary program for homeowners to mark and disavow covenants

quiz.q: What financial assistance does Washington State's Covenant Act provide to descendants of redlining victims?
quiz.explanation: Washington's Covenant Homeownership Act provides down payment assistance specifically to descendants of people excluded by racist housing covenants.

laws.title: Washington State CARE Act and Drug Treatment Alternative Law
laws.subtitle: Public Drug Use and Mental Health Diversion
laws.fullDescription: Creates a new legal framework for addressing public drug use and mental health crises, following the failure of recriminalization attempts. The law establishes CARE (Community Assistance, Recovery, and Empowerment) courts as civil diversion from criminal charges, mandates connection to treatment services, creates emergency response teams pairing mental health workers with police, and establishes treatment funding.
laws.penalty: CARE court orders for treatment compliance; civil penalties for persistent non-compliance
exceptions: Voluntary treatment participants have enhanced protections
Youth under 18 handled exclusively through youth services

quiz.q: What does the CARE in Washington's CARE Act stand for?
quiz.explanation: CARE stands for Community Assistance, Recovery, and Empowerment, reflecting Washington's approach to drug policy through treatment rather than incarceration.

laws.title: Clean Fuels Standard Expansion
laws.subtitle: Washington Accelerates Low-Carbon Transportation Fuels
laws.fullDescription: Washington State expanded its Clean Fuels Standard to require increasing percentages of low-carbon fuels in transportation, creating a market for clean fuel credits incentivizing biofuels, EV charging, and hydrogen.
laws.penalty: Fuel supplier fines for non-compliance
exceptions: Agricultural use exemptions
Small supplier thresholds

quiz.q: What does Washington State's Clean Fuels Standard require?
options: Increasing percentages of low-carbon fuels in transportation
quiz.explanation: Washington's Clean Fuels Standard requires increasing percentages of low-carbon fuels in transportation.
