laws.title: Blake Decision Response and Drug Possession Law
laws.subtitle: Washington Re-Criminalizes Drug Possession After Court Ruling
laws.fullDescription: After the state Supreme Court's 2021 Blake decision struck down Washington's drug possession law, the legislature enacted a replacement that criminalized simple possession as a misdemeanor. After debate over enforcement, a 2023 law made possession a gross misdemeanor with mandatory treatment referrals. The state continued refining its approach.
laws.penalty: Gross misdemeanor: up to 364 days and $5,000 fine; treatment referral required
exceptions: Treatment completion can result in charge dismissal
Diversion programs available

quiz.q: What court decision forced Washington to rewrite its drug possession law?
quiz.explanation: Washington's Supreme Court Blake decision in 2021 struck down the state's drug possession law, forcing the legislature to enact replacement legislation.

laws.title: Prescription Drug Affordability Board
laws.subtitle: Washington Creates Drug Price Review Authority
laws.fullDescription: Washington State established a Prescription Drug Affordability Board with authority to review high-cost drugs and potentially set upper payment limits for state-funded programs. Washington joined a growing number of states creating drug pricing oversight mechanisms as federal action lagged.
laws.penalty: Civil penalties for non-compliance with board determinations
exceptions: Innovative drug incentive protections
Small manufacturer exemptions

quiz.q: What power does Washington's Prescription Drug Affordability Board have?
options: Review high-cost drugs and potentially set upper payment limits
quiz.explanation: Washington's Prescription Drug Affordability Board can review high-cost drugs and set upper payment limits for state-funded programs.

laws.title: AI Accountability and Automated Decision Transparency
laws.subtitle: Washington Requires Explanation for Algorithmic Decisions
laws.fullDescription: Washington State enacted legislation requiring businesses using automated decision-making systems for employment, housing, credit, and similar high-stakes decisions to provide explanations upon request. The law also required impact assessments for high-risk AI and created a public registry of consequential automated decision systems.
laws.penalty: Civil fines for non-disclosure; attorney general enforcement
exceptions: Trade secret protections for model weights
Research and internal use exemptions

quiz.q: What does Washington State require businesses using automated decisions to provide?
options: Explanation of automated decisions upon request
quiz.explanation: Washington State requires businesses using automated decision-making in high-stakes areas to provide explanations of those decisions upon request.

laws.title: Salmon Recovery and Dam Removal
laws.subtitle: Snake River Dam Removal Aids Fish Recovery
laws.fullDescription: Washington State and federal agencies moved toward removing four lower Snake River dams, a historic decision to restore salmon runs. The dams generated electricity but significantly reduced salmon populations critical to Indigenous tribes and the fishing economy. The removal was the largest dam removal project in US history.
laws.penalty: No criminal penalties; environmental compliance for removal contractors
exceptions: Hydroelectric replacement power requirements
Tribal consultation requirements

quiz.q: Why were Snake River dams being considered for removal?
options: To restore salmon runs critical to Indigenous tribes and fishing
quiz.explanation: The lower Snake River dams were being considered for removal to restore salmon runs that are critical to Indigenous tribes and the broader fishing economy.

laws.title: Reproductive Rights and Abortion Refuge State
laws.subtitle: Washington Protects Out-of-State Abortion Seekers
laws.fullDescription: Washington State enacted comprehensive protections for abortion seekers including shield laws protecting doctors and patients from prosecution in other states, telehealth abortion across state lines, and a state-funded travel support program for low-income patients from restricted states.
laws.penalty: State laws protect against out-of-state subpoenas and warrants for abortion cases
exceptions: Federal law supremacy questions
Interstate legal conflict resolution

quiz.q: What do Washington State's shield laws protect?
options: Doctors and patients from prosecution in other states for abortion
quiz.explanation: Washington's shield laws protect abortion providers and patients from prosecution or civil suits brought by states with abortion restrictions.

laws.title: Salmon Recovery and Dam Removal on Klamath River
laws.subtitle: Largest dam removal in US history restores Pacific salmon runs
laws.fullDescription: The Klamath River dam removal project — the largest dam removal in US history — removed four dams to restore salmon migration. While the main Klamath dams were on the Oregon/California border, the project reflects a broader Pacific Northwest shift toward dam removal for salmon recovery. Washington State has multiple dam removal projects on rivers important to tribal salmon fishing rights. Tribes have treaty rights to salmon that predate US law, creating legal obligations for habitat restoration.
laws.penalty: Dam operators must conduct fish passage assessments; failure to provide adequate passage can trigger regulatory action
exceptions: Hydroelectric power generation needs are balanced against fish migration requirements
Small diversion dams for irrigation may use fish screens rather than removal

laws.title: Boeing Crisis and Aerospace Manufacturing Decline
laws.subtitle: Boeing's safety failures threaten Washington State's largest employer
laws.fullDescription: Boeing, Washington State's largest private employer, faces an existential crisis after the 737 MAX crashes (346 deaths) and door plug blowout on a 737 MAX 9 (2024). The FAA imposed production caps, executives resigned, and criminal investigations continued. Boeing's quality control failures were linked to cost-cutting after its merger with McDonnell Douglas. The 787 Dreamliner program moved production from Washington State to South Carolina. Washington State's aerospace ecosystem — suppliers, engineers, logistics — is threatened by Boeing's decline.
laws.penalty: FAA production caps limit Boeing's 737 MAX output until quality standards are met
exceptions: Defense contracts continue under separate military procurement regulations
787 Dreamliner and 777 production unaffected by 737 MAX-specific production caps

laws.title: Carbon Market and Climate Commitment Act
laws.subtitle: Washington's cap-and-invest carbon pricing generates billions for climate
laws.fullDescription: Washington State's Climate Commitment Act created a cap-and-invest carbon pricing program that auctions pollution allowances, generating billions for climate investments — transit, clean energy, salmon recovery, and wildfire prevention. The first auctions generated over $2 billion. Washington set a 2045 100% clean electricity target and 2035 new car sales must be electric. The program survived a ballot challenge in 2024. Washington's carbon market is the most ambitious state-level carbon pricing program in the US.
laws.penalty: Large industrial emitters must hold sufficient allowances to cover their emissions or face penalties
exceptions: Tribal nations have separate consultation process for activities affecting treaty resources
Agricultural operations exempt from direct carbon pricing requirements

quiz.q: What did Washington State's first carbon market auctions generate?
quiz.explanation: Washington State's Climate Commitment Act carbon auctions generated over $2 billion in the first years — invested in transit, clean energy, salmon recovery, and wildfire prevention across the state.

laws.title: Carbon Cap-and-Trade Program and Industrial Transition
laws.subtitle: Washington State's comprehensive climate cap-and-invest program
laws.fullDescription: Washington State launched its Climate Commitment Act (CCA) cap-and-invest program in 2023, becoming one of the few US states with a comprehensive carbon pricing system. The program caps greenhouse gas emissions from large polluters and requires them to purchase allowances, generating revenue invested in clean transportation, clean energy, and environmental justice programs. The CCA was designed to link eventually with California and Quebec's existing cap-and-trade systems, creating a larger carbon market. In November 2024, voters passed Initiative 2117 repealing the CCA, a significant setback for climate advocates. The repeal illustrated challenges of maintaining ambitious climate policies through direct democracy when costs are visible but climate benefits are diffuse. Washington had also passed major clean energy legislation requiring utilities to be carbon-free by 2045. The state is home to major tech companies (Amazon, Microsoft) with their own net-zero commitments that exist independently of state law.
laws.penalty: CCA violations (before repeal) carried significant fines; other Washington environmental laws carry their own penalties
exceptions: Agricultural activities had specific treatment under the CCA

quiz.q: What happened to Washington State's Climate Commitment Act cap-and-invest program in November 2024?
options: It was expanded to include more industries
Voters passed an initiative repealing it
It was linked with California's cap-and-trade system
It was replaced by a carbon tax
quiz.explanation: Washington State voters passed Initiative 2117 in November 2024, repealing the Climate Commitment Act cap-and-invest program — a significant setback showing the challenges of maintaining carbon pricing through direct democracy.

laws.title: Big Tech Headquarters and Employment Concentration
laws.subtitle: Washington State as home to Amazon, Microsoft, and tech ecosystem
laws.fullDescription: Washington State hosts the global headquarters of Amazon and Microsoft — two of the world's largest companies by market capitalization — and a dense ecosystem of tech companies, startups, and suppliers in the Seattle metropolitan area. The concentration has made Washington State one of the highest-income states in the US but also among the most economically unequal, with a tech-driven economy coexisting with significant unhoused populations and housing affordability crises. Amazon's HQ2 process (choosing a second headquarters location) created a bidding war between cities but also prompted backlash about corporate subsidies. Microsoft's investments in AI through its OpenAI partnership have made Redmond a global center for AI development. Washington has no state income tax, making it attractive for high-income tech workers. The state has passed its own data privacy law and has been a leader on digital rights policy.
laws.penalty: Washington State data privacy law (My Health MY Data Act, Washington Privacy Act) carry enforcement by the Attorney General; employment laws apply to tech workers
exceptions: Federal law preempts some state digital regulation in certain contexts

quiz.q: Which two of the world's largest technology companies are headquartered in Washington State?
quiz.explanation: Washington State hosts the global headquarters of both Amazon (in Seattle) and Microsoft (in Redmond) — two of the world's largest companies by market cap — creating one of the most concentrated tech ecosystems anywhere.

laws.title: Boeing Crisis and Aerospace Manufacturing Challenges
laws.subtitle: Washington State's flagship industry under severe quality pressure
laws.fullDescription: Washington State is home to Boeing's commercial aircraft manufacturing, historically one of the state's most important employers and economic drivers. Boeing has faced severe quality and safety crises — the two 737 MAX crashes in 2018-2019 killed 346 people and led to 20-month grounding of the aircraft, costing Boeing billions. In January 2024, a door panel blew out of an Alaska Airlines 737 MAX 9 in mid-flight, leading to further inspections and production limits imposed by the FAA. The FAA capped Boeing's 737 MAX production rate. Boeing moved its corporate headquarters from Chicago to Arlington, Virginia. The quality problems have been attributed to a corporate culture shift toward financial metrics over engineering excellence, outsourcing, and labor-management tensions. Boeing's machinists union went on strike in 2024. The crisis has affected suppliers throughout Washington State.
laws.penalty: FAA regulations carry significant fines for aviation safety violations; criminal charges can apply to negligent acts causing aircraft unsafe conditions
exceptions: Some testing and certification flights operate under specific FAA exemptions

quiz.q: What accident in January 2024 led to further FAA production limits on Boeing's 737 MAX?
options: A 737 MAX crash during landing in a snowstorm
A door panel blew out of an Alaska Airlines 737 MAX 9 in mid-flight
An engine failure during takeoff from Seattle
A runway collision between two 737 MAX aircraft
quiz.explanation: In January 2024, a door panel blew out of an Alaska Airlines 737 MAX 9 during flight, exposing passengers to near-fatal conditions and leading the FAA to cap Boeing's 737 MAX production rate pending quality reviews.

laws.title: Cap-and-Invest Climate Program
laws.subtitle: Washington's carbon market funds clean transportation
laws.fullDescription: Washington State launched its cap-and-invest program in 2023, requiring large emitters to purchase allowances for carbon emissions and using the revenue for clean transportation, energy efficiency and environmental justice programs. The program initially raised gasoline prices, fueling a ballot initiative to repeal it which passed in November 2024. The repeal eliminated the program in 2025, setting back Washington's climate ambitions and creating a cautionary tale about the political sustainability of carbon pricing.
laws.penalty: Large emitters must purchase allowances for covered emissions; non-compliance subject to significant financial penalties
exceptions: Small businesses below emission thresholds exempt
Agricultural operations have specific emission exclusions

quiz.q: What happened to Washington State's cap-and-invest climate program in November 2024?
options: It was transferred to the federal government
quiz.explanation: Washington voters passed a ballot initiative in November 2024 to repeal the cap-and-invest program, which had initially raised gasoline prices, setting back the state's climate ambitions in a cautionary tale about carbon pricing politics.

laws.title: Microsoft AI Ethics Framework
laws.subtitle: Seattle tech giant develops voluntary AI responsibility standards
laws.fullDescription: Microsoft, headquartered in Redmond, Washington, has developed one of the most comprehensive voluntary AI ethics frameworks in the technology industry. Its Responsible AI standard includes fairness, reliability, privacy, security, inclusiveness, transparency and accountability principles. Microsoft's $10 billion investment in OpenAI made it central to the generative AI revolution. Washington State has benefited economically from Microsoft's growth while also facing questions about whether voluntary corporate AI ethics frameworks are sufficient without government regulation.
laws.penalty: Microsoft's internal AI ethics violations handled through internal governance; external regulatory frameworks emerging
exceptions: National security AI applications subject to government oversight
Research and development has broader freedom than commercial deployment

quiz.q: How much did Microsoft invest in OpenAI as part of its generative AI strategy?
quiz.explanation: Microsoft invested $10 billion in OpenAI, making it central to the generative AI revolution and integrating AI capabilities across its products including Azure, Office, Windows and Bing.

laws.title: Boeing Crisis and Manufacturing Collapse
laws.subtitle: Boeing's quality failures devastate Pacific Northwest aerospace
laws.fullDescription: Boeing, headquartered in Chicago but manufacturing in Everett, Washington, suffered a series of quality and safety crises. The Alaska Airlines door plug blowout in January 2024 on a 737 MAX 9 triggered federal investigations revealing systemic quality control failures. The FAA limited production rates. A 53-day machinist strike disrupted production. New CEO Kelly Ortberg implemented turnaround measures. Boeing's crisis devastated its supplier network in Washington State and threatened America's largest manufacturing exporter.
laws.penalty: FAA production caps limit 737 MAX output; Boeing faces enhanced regulatory oversight with mandatory quality audits
exceptions: Defense contracts continue under separate certification
Existing delivered aircraft can continue operating after inspection

quiz.q: What Boeing incident in January 2024 triggered federal investigations into systemic quality failures?
options: 737 MAX 9 door plug blowout on an Alaska Airlines flight
quiz.explanation: A door plug blowout on an Alaska Airlines Boeing 737 MAX 9 in January 2024 triggered FAA investigations that revealed systemic quality control failures at Boeing's factories, leading to production caps and enhanced regulatory oversight.

laws.title: Cap-and-Invest Climate Program
laws.subtitle: Western US Carbon Market
laws.fullDescription: Washington State launched its cap-and-invest program in 2023, one of only three such programs in North America. Large industrial emitters and fuel suppliers must purchase allowances for their emissions, with the cap declining each year. Revenue — projected to be billions over the program's life — funds electric vehicle rebates, public transit, wildfire resilience, and clean energy access for low-income communities. Washington links its market with California and Quebec, creating the Western Climate Initiative.
laws.penalty: Penalties up to $10,000 per day per violation; $44,000 per metric ton of uncovered emissions
exceptions: Facilities emitting below 25,000 metric tons CO2 equivalent annually
Agricultural operations
Federally recognized tribes

laws.title: Washington State Vaccine Mandate for Healthcare Workers
laws.subtitle: Immunization for Patient Protection
laws.fullDescription: Washington State requires healthcare workers at licensed healthcare facilities to be vaccinated against influenza and COVID-19, with the COVID requirement upheld after significant controversy in 2021. Washington also has strong childhood immunization requirements for school attendance. The state's vaccine exemption process was tightened in 2019 after a measles outbreak in Clark County, limiting personal belief exemptions and requiring healthcare provider consultation. Washington's vaccine laws balance public health protection with medical accommodation.
laws.penalty: Unvaccinated healthcare workers may be terminated; schools may exclude unvaccinated children; fines for facilities not tracking compliance
exceptions: Medical exemptions from licensed healthcare providers
Religious exemptions under federal EEOC Title VII for employees

laws.title: Washington Long-Term Services Insurance
laws.subtitle: WA Cares Fund — First State Long-Term Care
laws.fullDescription: Washington State created the nation's first mandatory long-term care insurance program: WA Cares Fund. Workers contribute 0.58% of wages (no employer match) and earn up to $36,500 in lifetime benefits for long-term care needs (home care, assisted living, nursing home). Long-term care is uninsured for most Americans — Medicaid only covers it after spending down savings. Washington's model addresses this coverage gap. The program faced controversy over its opt-out provisions and self-employed exemptions but is now operational. Washington also has a $16.28/hour minimum wage (2024), among the nation's highest.
laws.penalty: Non-compliant employers: premium liability plus interest; workers who opt out lose benefits; payroll deduction mandatory
exceptions: Self-employed can voluntarily opt in
Veterans with service-connected disabilities may be exempt

laws.title: Washington State Promise Scholarship
laws.subtitle: Community College Access
laws.fullDescription: Washington State's Promise Scholarship provides free tuition and fees for eligible students at community and technical colleges — focused on recent high school graduates from lower-income families. Washington has the Washington Student Achievement Council managing financial aid. The state's K-12 system was the subject of the landmark McCleary v. Washington Supreme Court case, which found the state violated its constitutional duty to provide basic education and ordered increased funding. Washington has among the strongest teacher collective bargaining rights. The state is also a national leader in career and technical education pathways.
laws.penalty: Schools receiving state funding must comply with performance and equity standards; teacher certification requirements enforced
exceptions: Private schools under different funding framework
Homeschool families have alternative compliance routes

laws.title: Keep Washington Working Act
laws.subtitle: Washington's immigrant protection and data privacy
laws.fullDescription: Washington's Keep Washington Working Act (2019) restricts state and local agencies from using public resources to assist federal civil immigration enforcement and prohibits sharing certain data with immigration authorities. Washington provides driver's licenses to undocumented residents and extends in-state tuition to undocumented students. The state created the Immigrant and Refugee Commission to advise the Governor. Washington's agricultural economy employs hundreds of thousands of undocumented workers, giving the state economic incentives for protection policies.
laws.penalty: State agencies violating the Act by improperly sharing immigrant data or assisting civil immigration enforcement face administrative consequences; attorney general may enforce compliance
exceptions: Law enforcement may respond to criminal warrants regardless of immigration implications
Cooperation allowed in cases involving serious felonies
laws.sourceLabel: Washington Keep Washington Working Act RCW 43.06C

quiz.q: Washington State's Keep Washington Working Act was motivated in part by the state's economic dependence on undocumented workers in which sector?
quiz.explanation: Washington's large agricultural sector—apple orchards, berry farms, vineyards—relies heavily on undocumented immigrant labor. This economic reality shaped the state's protective immigration policies, as farmers and food processors lobbied against strict enforcement measures.

laws.title: Initiative 502: Cannabis Legalization Pioneer
laws.subtitle: Washington's groundbreaking 2012 marijuana legalization
laws.fullDescription: Washington State's Initiative 502 (2012) was one of the first two US states (alongside Colorado) to legalize recreational cannabis, pioneering the regulatory model later adopted by other states. Washington's Liquor and Cannabis Board oversees the market. Washington State has been innovative in drug policy: the Supreme Court struck down simple drug possession laws in 2021 (Blake decision), temporarily decriminalizing possession — the legislature responded with a new simple possession misdemeanor. Washington also created supervised consumption sites in King County.
laws.penalty: Cannabis possession over 1 oz (28.5g): misdemeanor; cannabis delivery without license: felony; heroin/cocaine possession: gross misdemeanor (post-Blake); trafficking controlled substances: felony with mandatory minimums
exceptions: Adults 21+ may possess up to 1 oz cannabis flower, 16 oz infused solid, 72 oz infused liquid, 7 grams concentrate
Medical cannabis authorization allows higher possession amounts
laws.sourceLabel: Washington State Initiative 502 and Cannabis Licensing

quiz.q: Washington's 2021 Blake decision temporarily had what effect on simple drug possession?
options: Made all drug possession a federal matter
Decriminalized simple drug possession by striking down the state law
quiz.explanation: In State v. Blake (2021), Washington's Supreme Court struck down the state's simple drug possession law as unconstitutional (it lacked a knowledge element), temporarily making drug possession not a crime in Washington. The legislature then passed a new law making possession a misdemeanor.

laws.title: Washington State LGBTQ+ Rights
laws.subtitle: Washington's strong LGBTQ+ protections
laws.fullDescription: Washington State has broad LGBTQ+ protections. Washington voters approved same-sex marriage by referendum in 2012 (Referendum 74) — one of the first states to approve marriage equality by popular vote. Washington State has a Law Against Discrimination that covers sexual orientation and gender expression. Washington bans conversion therapy for minors. Washington State was among the first to add gender identity to anti-discrimination laws. Washington Governor Jay Inslee established the Governor's Interagency Council on Health Disparities to address LGBTQ+ health inequities.
laws.penalty: LGBTQ+ discrimination in employment, housing, public accommodation: civil liability and administrative investigation; hate crimes: enhanced felony penalties; conversion therapy on minors by licensed therapists: license revocation
exceptions: Religious organizations retain some employment exemptions for coreligionist matters
State law doesn't explicitly cover all small employers in all contexts
laws.sourceLabel: Washington State Human Rights Commission LGBTQ+ Protections

quiz.q: Washington State's 2012 Referendum 74 was notable because it was one of the first times US voters did what?
options: Approved same-sex marriage by popular vote (ballot referendum)
Approved adoption rights for same-sex couples
quiz.explanation: Washington's Referendum 74 in November 2012 — along with Maine and Maryland on the same night — was one of the first times that voters directly approved same-sex marriage in a US state, rather than it being legislatively or judicially enacted.

laws.title: Journalist Shield Act and Media Diversity
laws.subtitle: Washington State has a strong shield law and diverse media landscape
laws.fullDescription: Washington's Shield Act (RCW 5.68.010) provides qualified privilege for journalists against compelled disclosure of sources or unpublished information. Washington has strong public disclosure laws under the Public Records Act. The state is home to major tech journalism and investigative outlets. Washington journalists have used shield protections to protect sources in major investigative stories. Washington's anti-SLAPP law provides additional protection. Seattle is a significant journalism hub with an active independent media scene. The state has shown support for press freedom in public policy.
laws.penalty: Journalists have qualified privilege against source disclosure; SLAPP suits face early dismissal
exceptions: A party may overcome the privilege by showing compelling need and exhaustion of other means

quiz.q: What must a party show to overcome Washington's journalist shield protection?
options: Compelling need and exhaustion of other means
quiz.explanation: Washington's Shield Act provides qualified privilege that can be overcome if a party demonstrates a compelling need for the information and that all other means of obtaining it have been exhausted — a high bar that provides meaningful protection.

laws.title: My Health MY Data Act and Consumer Privacy Protections
laws.subtitle: Washington has strong health data privacy protections covering social media-collected health information
laws.fullDescription: Washington passed the My Health MY Data Act (2023), providing broad protections for consumer health data collected by entities not covered by HIPAA — including data collected through apps, social media platforms, and wearable devices. The law has a private right of action. Washington also has the Washington Privacy Act (WPA, 2021) covering facial recognition. Washington's Consumer Protection Act is used against unfair digital practices. Washington has been an active regulator of tech companies given its position as home to Microsoft, Amazon, and major cloud providers.
laws.penalty: MHMD Act violations subject to Consumer Protection Act penalties; private right of action for violations
exceptions: HIPAA-covered entities are exempt from the MHMD Act

quiz.q: What type of health data does Washington's My Health MY Data Act protect that federal HIPAA does not cover?
options: Consumer health data collected by apps, social media, and wearables
quiz.explanation: Washington's My Health MY Data Act (2023) protects consumer health data collected by entities not covered by HIPAA — including data from apps, social media platforms, and wearable devices that track health information outside the traditional healthcare system.

laws.title: Washington's Money Transmitter Law and Fintech Regulation
laws.subtitle: Washington regulates money transmission including for digital assets and remittances
laws.fullDescription: Washington State regulates money transmitters through the Uniform Money Services Act, requiring licenses for businesses transmitting money including cryptocurrency exchanges and remittance services. The Washington State Department of Financial Institutions (DFI) oversees banking and financial services. Washington is home to Microsoft, Amazon, and major tech companies with financial service arms that require state licensing. Washington's credit unions serve diverse communities. The state has consumer protection rules for predatory lending. Washington has a significant remittance market serving Mexican, Filipino, and other immigrant communities.
laws.penalty: Unlicensed money transmission is a felony; DFI can impose fines and revoke licenses
exceptions: Banks and trust companies licensed by federal authorities are exempt

quiz.q: What law requires Washington State licensing for cryptocurrency exchanges and remittance services?
quiz.explanation: Washington State's Uniform Money Services Act requires any business transmitting money — including cryptocurrency exchanges and remittance services — to obtain a state license, ensuring consumer protection and anti-money laundering compliance for a wide range of financial services.

laws.title: Washington State Animal Care and Control Laws
laws.subtitle: Strong felony cruelty statutes and orca-linked animal protections
laws.fullDescription: Washington RCW 16.52 governs animal cruelty. First-degree animal cruelty (intentional torture or killing) is a Class C felony. Second-degree cruelty (neglect, abandonment) is a gross misdemeanor. Washington expanded protections in 2018 to include 'companion animal' cruelty reporting obligations for veterinarians — vets who suspect abuse may report to law enforcement without client consent, similar to mandatory reporting for child abuse. Washington also has extensive orca protection laws that interact with marine mammal welfare (see separate orca laws). Pet shops must source from shelters/rescues under Seattle ordinance. Equine welfare is also addressed under RCW 16.52.
laws.penalty: Class C felony (animal cruelty 1st degree): up to 5 years and $10,000 fine; gross misdemeanor (2nd degree): up to 364 days and $5,000 fine; animal fighting: Class C felony
exceptions: Customary agricultural practices including branding, dehorning, castration
Research facilities under IACUC
Wildlife managed by WDFW

quiz.q: What professional reporting obligation did Washington State create in 2018 regarding animal abuse?
options: Mandatory reporting by animal control officers
Veterinarians may report suspected animal abuse without client consent
Pet store owners must report all bite incidents
Shelters must report capacity issues to courts
quiz.explanation: Washington's 2018 law allows veterinarians to report suspected companion animal abuse to law enforcement without the client's consent — modeled on mandatory reporter laws for child abuse — a significant animal welfare protection.

laws.title: Washington State Community Property and Parenting Act
laws.subtitle: Washington's 2021 Uniform Parentage Act modernizes family law
laws.fullDescription: Washington is a community property state. Washington enacted the Uniform Parentage Act in 2021, modernizing parentage law to reflect contemporary family structures including same-sex couples, assisted reproduction, and de facto parents. The Act protects the rights of de facto parents (non-biological/non-adoptive individuals who've acted as parents). Washington requires a Parenting Plan in all cases involving children — a detailed document addressing custody, decision-making, and dispute resolution. Washington courts strongly favor joint custody arrangements. Domestic Violence: Washington has extensive protections including Domestic Violence Protection Orders and sexual assault protections. Washington was among the first states to legalize same-sex marriage (2012 referendum).
laws.penalty: Contempt for violating parenting plans: fines, modification proceedings; child support non-compliance: wage garnishment, licence suspension, contempt; DV violations: criminal charges
exceptions: Prenuptial agreements
Separate property
Tribal family law for tribal members on reservations

quiz.q: What new category of parental rights did Washington's 2021 Uniform Parentage Act create protections for?
options: De facto parents — non-biological individuals who have functioned as parents
quiz.explanation: Washington's 2021 Uniform Parentage Act specifically protects de facto parents — people who aren't biological or adoptive parents but have functioned in a parental role. This protects children's relationships with step-parents, same-sex partners, and others who have parented them, regardless of legal or biological status.

laws.title: Washington State Landlord-Tenant Act & Just Cause Eviction
laws.subtitle: 2021 just-cause eviction requirements statewide
laws.fullDescription: Washington's Residential Landlord-Tenant Act (RCW 59.18) was significantly strengthened by SB 5160 (2021), which requires landlords to have 'just cause' for evicting month-to-month tenants. Allowed just causes include nonpayment of rent, violation of lease terms, and the landlord's intent to sell or occupy the unit. The law also requires 20-day notice for month-to-month termination. Seattle and other cities have additional local protections. Washington does not have statewide rent control.
laws.penalty: Wrongful eviction: tenant entitled to actual damages, court costs, and attorney fees
exceptions: Just cause required for tenants on month-to-month after initial lease term
Owner move-in requires 90-day notice

quiz.q: What major tenant protection did Washington's SB 5160 (2021) introduce?
quiz.explanation: SB 5160 (2021) introduced a statewide just-cause eviction requirement, meaning landlords must have a legally recognized reason (like nonpayment or lease violation) to evict month-to-month tenants after the initial lease term ends.

laws.title: Washington Consumer Protection Act & My Health MY Data Act
laws.subtitle: Consumer protection and pioneering health data law
laws.fullDescription: Washington's Consumer Protection Act (CPA, RCW 19.86) prohibits unfair or deceptive acts in commerce with private right of action for actual damages, costs, and attorney fees. The 2023 My Health MY Data Act (MHMDA) is the nation's strongest health data privacy law — it applies to any entity that collects health data on Washington residents (not just HIPAA-covered entities) and requires affirmative consent before collection, prohibiting geofencing near healthcare facilities. The Washington Data Breach Notification Law requires notification within 30 days. Washington is also known for its strong Lemon Law and Home Inspector Licensing Act.
laws.penalty: CPA violation: actual damages + attorney fees; MHMDA violation: private right of action similar to CPA
exceptions: MHMDA covers health data beyond HIPAA — including period tracker apps
30-day data breach notification requirement
laws.source: RCW 19.86 (CPA); My Health MY Data Act (2023)
laws.sourceLabel: Washington My Health MY Data Act

quiz.q: What makes Washington's 2023 My Health MY Data Act broader than federal HIPAA health data rules?
options: It applies to all residents of any state
It covers any entity collecting health data on WA residents, not just HIPAA-covered healthcare providers
It bans all digital health data collection
It requires encryption of all health apps
quiz.explanation: Washington's My Health MY Data Act (2023) extends health data privacy protections beyond HIPAA to cover any entity collecting health data on Washington residents — including period tracker apps, wellness platforms, and retail pharmacies not covered by HIPAA.

laws.title: Recreational Cannabis — I-502 (2012)
laws.subtitle: Initiative 502 — First state to legalize
laws.fullDescription: Washington was one of the first two states to legalize recreational cannabis in 2012. Adults 21+ may possess up to 1 oz marijuana, 16 oz infused solids, or 72 oz infused liquids. Licensed retail stores sell cannabis. Home cultivation remains prohibited for recreational users. Washington's 37% excise tax funds education and health.
laws.penalty: Possession over limits: misdemeanor. Under 21 possession: class 1 civil infraction ($100).
exceptions: Medical cannabis patients may home-grow up to 6 plants
Employment drug testing still permitted
DUI for cannabis still illegal
laws.sourceLabel: Washington State Liquor and Cannabis Board

quiz.q: Is home cultivation of cannabis for recreational use legal in Washington State?
options: No, home cultivation is prohibited for recreational users
quiz.explanation: Washington's recreational cannabis law (I-502) does not allow home cultivation. Only medical cannabis patients are permitted to grow up to 6 plants.

laws.title: Death Penalty Abolished (2023)
laws.subtitle: Washington RCW 10.95 — No executions since 2010
laws.fullDescription: Washington's Supreme Court declared the death penalty unconstitutional in 2018. In 2023, the legislature formally abolished it and converted all death sentences to life without parole. Washington had not carried out an execution since 2010. Governor Inslee imposed a moratorium in 2014.
laws.penalty: N/A — death penalty no longer exists. Murder: life without parole is maximum.
exceptions: Federal death penalty cases not affected by state abolition
Existing life without parole sentences continue
All prior death sentences converted to LWOP

quiz.q: What happened to existing death row sentences when Washington abolished the death penalty?
options: Sentences were commuted to time served
Sentences converted to life without parole
quiz.explanation: When Washington abolished the death penalty in 2023, all existing death row sentences were automatically converted to life without parole (LWOP).

laws.title: Paid Family and Medical Leave — Up to 18 Weeks
laws.subtitle: Washington PFML — Up to 90% wage replacement
laws.fullDescription: Washington's Paid Family and Medical Leave (PFML) program, which began in 2020, provides up to 12 weeks paid medical leave and 12 weeks family leave (up to 18 combined in some cases). Benefits replace up to 90% of wages for lower earners. Funded by employee and employer payroll premiums.
laws.penalty: Employers who interfere with PFML rights: civil penalties, back pay, damages.
exceptions: Self-employed may opt in voluntarily
Small employers (under 50) not required to pay employer premium
Federal and tribal workers have separate rules

quiz.q: When did Washington State's PFML program begin paying benefits?
quiz.explanation: Washington's PFML program began collecting premiums in 2019 and started paying benefits in January 2020, providing up to 90% wage replacement for qualifying events.

laws.title: Clean Electricity — Carbon-Free by 2030 (CETA)
laws.subtitle: Washington Clean Energy Transformation Act
laws.fullDescription: Washington's CETA (2019) requires utilities to eliminate coal from power supply by 2025 and be carbon-neutral by 2030, with 100% clean electricity by 2045. Washington already has one of the cleanest grids in the US (over 70% hydroelectric). The Climate Commitment Act (2021) added a cap-and-trade system.
laws.penalty: Utilities not meeting CETA standards face UTC fines.
exceptions: Small utilities have modified timelines
Hydroelectric power counts as clean under CETA
Some backup generation allowed for reliability

quiz.q: By what year must Washington utilities achieve 100% clean electricity under CETA?
quiz.explanation: Washington's CETA requires carbon neutrality by 2030 and 100% clean electricity by 2045. Washington's grid is already among the nation's cleanest with over 70% hydroelectric power.

laws.title: Zero Emission Vehicle Mandate — 2035
laws.subtitle: Washington Clean Cars 2030 — No new gas cars
laws.fullDescription: Washington adopted California's Advanced Clean Cars II standard, requiring all new passenger vehicles sold to be zero-emission by 2035. Washington's EV adoption rate is among the nation's highest. The state offers reduced registration fees for EVs and has invested heavily in charging infrastructure.
laws.penalty: Automakers not meeting ZEV sales targets face compliance costs.
exceptions: Used cars not affected
Emergency and specialty vehicles have exemptions
Plug-in hybrids may have a transition period

quiz.q: By what year must all new passenger vehicles sold in Washington be zero-emission?
quiz.explanation: Washington adopted the 2035 ZEV mandate requiring all new passenger cars and light trucks sold in the state to be zero-emission, following California's Advanced Clean Cars II standard.

laws.title: Reproductive Privacy Act — Codified 1991
laws.subtitle: Washington RCW 9.02 — Pre-Dobbs abortion rights
laws.fullDescription: Washington codified abortion rights in state law as early as 1991 following a voter initiative. The Reproductive Privacy Act guarantees the right to abortion before fetal viability and after viability when necessary to protect the mother's health. Washington does not require parental consent for minors. After Dobbs, Washington added shield laws.
laws.penalty: N/A — This protects access to abortion.
exceptions: Healthcare providers may conscientiously object but must refer
No gestational limit in state law when medically necessary
No parental consent requirement for minors

quiz.q: When did Washington State first codify abortion rights into state law?
quiz.explanation: Washington voters approved a 1991 initiative codifying abortion rights in state law, making Washington well-prepared when the Supreme Court overturned Roe in 2022.

laws.title: No State Income Tax — B&O Tax Instead
laws.subtitle: Washington Constitution — Zero income tax
laws.fullDescription: Washington has no state income tax. Instead, businesses pay a Business & Occupation (B&O) tax on gross receipts, regardless of profit. This makes Washington friendly for high-income workers but potentially burdensome for low-margin businesses. In 2021, a capital gains tax on gains over $250K was passed.
laws.penalty: B&O tax violations: interest, penalties, and potential audit.
exceptions: Federal income tax applies
Capital gains tax (over $250K) applies to certain investment sales
Sales tax (10.1% in Seattle) applies

quiz.q: What type of tax do Washington businesses pay instead of a conventional income tax?
options: Business & Occupation (B&O) tax on gross receipts
quiz.explanation: Washington businesses pay a Business & Occupation (B&O) tax on gross receipts (revenue), not profit. Businesses pay even if they're not profitable.

laws.title: Universal Background Checks — I-594 (2014)
laws.subtitle: Initiative 594 — Background check on all gun sales
laws.fullDescription: Washington's I-594 (2014) requires background checks for all firearm sales and transfers, including private sales. In 2018, I-1639 raised the purchase age for semi-automatic rifles to 21 and created secure storage requirements. Washington's gun laws are among the stricter in the Western US.
laws.penalty: Transferring without background check: class C felony. Negligent storage: misdemeanor.
exceptions: Gifts between immediate family members may be exempt
Law enforcement transfers exempt
Antique firearms (pre-1899) generally exempt

quiz.q: Under Washington's I-594, when is a background check required for firearm transfers?
options: For all sales and transfers, including private
quiz.explanation: Washington's I-594 (2014) requires background checks for ALL firearm sales and transfers, including private sales between individuals — closing the 'gun show loophole.'

laws.title: LGBTQ+ Non-Discrimination Laws — Comprehensive
laws.subtitle: Washington Law Against Discrimination — RCW 49.60
laws.fullDescription: Washington State has comprehensive anti-discrimination protections covering sexual orientation and gender identity in employment, housing, credit, and public accommodations. Washington was among the first states to add gender identity (2006). Washington voters approved same-sex marriage in 2012 by popular vote.
laws.penalty: Discrimination violations: Human Rights Commission enforcement, civil lawsuits, attorney's fees.
exceptions: Religious organizations have some hiring exemptions
Bona fide occupational qualification defense
Small employers may have limited exemptions

quiz.q: When did Washington add gender identity to its anti-discrimination law?
quiz.explanation: Washington State added gender identity and expression to its Law Against Discrimination in 2006, making it one of the first states to explicitly protect transgender individuals.

laws.title: Just Cause Eviction — Landlord-Tenant Reform (2021)
laws.subtitle: Washington RCW 59.18 — Just cause required
laws.fullDescription: Washington strengthened tenant protections in 2021 with just cause eviction requirements for month-to-month tenants. Landlords must have a valid reason (non-payment, lease violation, property sale, etc.) to end tenancy. Seattle has even stronger tenant protections.
laws.penalty: Illegal eviction (self-help eviction): damages including wrongful eviction damages.
exceptions: Landlords may evict for legitimate lease violations
Property sales may trigger eviction with proper notice
Week-to-week tenancies have different rules

quiz.q: Under Washington's 2021 landlord-tenant reforms, what must landlords generally show to evict month-to-month tenants?
quiz.explanation: Washington's 2021 reforms require landlords to have just cause (a valid legal reason from a statutory list) to terminate month-to-month tenancies, ending 'no-fault' evictions.

laws.title: Pacific Salmon Recovery — Snake River Dam Debate
laws.subtitle: Washington salmon recovery and treaty rights
laws.fullDescription: Washington has major salmon recovery programs due to declining salmon runs. The four lower Snake River dams are controversial — breaching them would aid salmon but remove ~8% of Pacific Northwest electricity. Native tribes view salmon recovery as treaty rights. Governor Inslee supported dam removal.
laws.penalty: Violations of Endangered Species Act protections: federal fines, project shutdowns.
exceptions: Treaty fishing rights for tribal nations recognized
Hatcheries supplement natural populations
Columbia River dams governed separately by federal compact

quiz.q: Why are the four Snake River dams controversial in Washington State?
options: They block salmon migration while providing significant electricity
quiz.explanation: The four lower Snake River dams block salmon migration critical for recovery of endangered runs, but removing them would eliminate approximately 8% of the Pacific Northwest's electricity.

laws.title: Hospital Nurse Staffing Ratios — SB 5236 (2023)
laws.subtitle: Washington — Mandatory staffing law
laws.fullDescription: Washington's SB 5236 (2023) established minimum nurse-to-patient ratios in hospitals, making Washington one of only two states (with California) with mandatory staffing laws. Emergency departments: 1 nurse to 4 patients. ICU: 1:2. Medical-surgical: 1:4–5. Takes effect in phases through 2026.
laws.penalty: Hospital violations: civil penalties, public disclosure.
exceptions: Some critical access hospitals have modified timelines
Certain specialty units may have adjusted ratios
Surge situations have emergency flexibility

quiz.q: What is the emergency department nurse-to-patient ratio required by Washington's 2023 staffing law?
quiz.explanation: Washington's SB 5236 requires emergency departments to maintain a 1:4 nurse-to-patient ratio, making Washington one of only two states mandating minimum nursing ratios.

laws.title: My Health My Data Act (2023) — Health Data Privacy
laws.subtitle: Washington health data protection beyond HIPAA
laws.fullDescription: Washington's My Health My Data Act (2023) protects health data collected by non-covered entities (apps, retailers, tech companies). Companies must obtain consent before collecting health data, cannot sell it without permission, and must honor deletion requests. Location data near healthcare facilities is protected.
laws.penalty: Private right of action for violations: damages, injunctive relief. AG enforcement: fines.
exceptions: HIPAA-covered entities regulated separately
De-identified/aggregate data may have different rules
Research with IRB oversight has modified requirements
laws.sourceLabel: Washington My Health My Data Act

quiz.q: What new type of location data does Washington's My Health My Data Act protect?
quiz.explanation: Washington's My Health My Data Act specifically protects location data collected near healthcare facilities, acknowledging that such location data can infer sensitive health conditions.

laws.title: Undocumented Immigrant Driver's Licenses
laws.subtitle: Washington RCW 46.20 — License regardless of status
laws.fullDescription: Washington allows undocumented immigrants to obtain state driver's licenses (non-REAL ID designated). Applicants must show identity, Washington residency, and pass driving tests. Washington joined about 20 states with such laws to increase road safety through licensed and insured drivers.
laws.penalty: Driving without a license (any driver): fine and possible vehicle impound.
exceptions: REAL ID and federal benefits require citizenship/legal status documentation
Non-REAL ID licenses marked as not for federal purposes
Some federal facilities require REAL ID

quiz.q: What can undocumented immigrants in Washington State obtain with proof of identity and residency?
quiz.explanation: Washington State allows undocumented immigrants to obtain state driver's licenses (designated as non-REAL ID) by proving their identity and Washington residency plus passing driving tests.

laws.title: Police Reform Package — 2021 Use-of-Force Standards
laws.subtitle: Washington SB 5476 & HB 1310 — 'Necessary' force standard
laws.fullDescription: Washington passed landmark police reform legislation in 2021: SB 5476 limited use of force to when 'necessary' (not just 'reasonable'), restricting neck restraints and vehicle pursuits. HB 1054 bans no-knock warrants and chokeholds. Some provisions were modified in 2022 after law enforcement concerns.
laws.penalty: Officers violating use of force policies: administrative discipline, decertification, civil liability.
exceptions: Life-threatening situations justify higher force levels
Warrant service with judicial approval may allow more tactics
2022 amendments restored some pursuit authority

quiz.q: Under Washington's 2021 SB 5476, police may only use force when it is?
quiz.explanation: Washington's SB 5476 raised the use-of-force standard from 'reasonable' to 'necessary' — one of the highest standards in the US.

laws.title: Forest Practices Act — Riparian Buffer Rules
laws.subtitle: Washington Forest Practices Act — Salmon habitat protection
laws.fullDescription: Washington's Forest Practices Act requires timber companies to leave forested buffer zones along streams and rivers to protect salmon habitat and water quality. Washington has one of the most comprehensive forest practice regulatory systems in the US, balancing timber harvest with environmental protection.
laws.penalty: Forest practice violations: stop-harvest orders, civil penalties up to $10,000/day.
exceptions: Small forest landowners have modified requirements
Certain small streams may have reduced buffer requirements
Salvage logging after fire has special provisions

quiz.q: What is the primary ecological purpose of riparian buffer zones in Washington's Forest Practices Act?
options: Protecting salmon habitat and water quality
quiz.explanation: Washington's riparian management zones are primarily designed to protect salmon habitat and water quality by filtering runoff, providing shade to cool water temperatures, and maintaining streambanks.

laws.title: Drug Decriminalization — Blake Decision (2021)
laws.subtitle: State v. Blake — Felony possession struck down
laws.fullDescription: Washington's Supreme Court (State v. Blake, 2021) struck down the state's felony drug possession law as unconstitutional because it didn't require knowing possession. The legislature temporarily created a misdemeanor possession law. In 2023, Washington passed a new law prioritizing treatment referrals over prosecution.
laws.penalty: Drug possession: gross misdemeanor with diversion to treatment encouraged.
exceptions: Distribution and trafficking still serious felonies
Drug courts and diversion programs available
Law enforcement may issue civil referrals before criminal charges

quiz.q: What did the Washington Supreme Court rule in State v. Blake (2021)?
options: The felony drug possession law was unconstitutional because it didn't require knowing possession
quiz.explanation: State v. Blake struck down Washington's felony drug possession law because it didn't require that the defendant knowingly possessed drugs, violating due process.

laws.title: Seattle Sugar-Sweetened Beverage Tax — $0.0175/oz
laws.subtitle: Seattle SMC 5.53 — Soda tax funding education
laws.fullDescription: Seattle charges a tax of 1.75 cents per ounce on sugar-sweetened beverages sold in the city, applying to sodas, energy drinks, and sweetened juices. Revenue funds early childhood education and nutrition programs. Implemented in 2018, Seattle joined a handful of US cities with such taxes.
laws.penalty: Non-compliant distributors: tax plus interest and penalties.
exceptions: Diet/zero-sugar drinks exempt
Milk-based beverages exempt
100% fruit juice exempt
laws.sourceLabel: City of Seattle — Sweetened Beverage Tax

quiz.q: At what rate does Seattle tax sugar-sweetened beverages per ounce?
quiz.explanation: Seattle's sweetened beverage tax is 1.75 cents ($0.0175) per ounce. Revenue goes to early childhood education and nutrition programs.

laws.title: Shoreline Management Act — 200-Foot Buffer
laws.subtitle: Washington Shoreline Management Act
laws.fullDescription: Washington's Shoreline Management Act (SMA) protects shorelines of state waters. New development within 200 feet of shorelines requires a Shoreline Substantial Development Permit. Local governments must create Shoreline Master Programs. Washington prioritizes public access and natural resource protection.
laws.penalty: Violations: stop-work orders, fines, restoration requirements.
exceptions: Single-family homes may qualify for Shoreline Exemptions
Agricultural activities on existing farm lands
Minor repairs to existing lawful structures

quiz.q: What is the protected shoreline buffer distance under Washington's Shoreline Management Act?
quiz.explanation: Washington's Shoreline Management Act establishes a 200-foot buffer from shorelines of state waters where development requires permits.

laws.title: All-Mail Voting — Washington's Model System
laws.subtitle: Washington Elections Code — Universal mail ballot
laws.fullDescription: Washington pioneered all-mail voting — every registered voter automatically receives a ballot by mail before each election. Ballots can be returned by mail or dropped at drop boxes. Voters can also vote in-person. Washington consistently has among the highest voter turnout rates in the US.
laws.penalty: Voter fraud: class C felony.
exceptions: Voters may opt to always vote in person if preferred
Overseas and military voters use UOCAVA rules
Same-day registration available at polling locations

quiz.q: What does Washington do with all registered voters before each election?
quiz.explanation: Washington automatically mails a ballot to every registered voter before each election. This all-mail system has produced consistently high voter turnout rates.
